bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 起閼逢困敦，盡重光協洽，凡八年。

translations.literal: From Quefeng Kundun through Chongguang Xieqia; eight years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Quefeng Kundun through Chongguang Xieqia—eight years in all.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，丁酉晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: 1. In winter, the tenth month, on the last day dingyou, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In winter, the tenth month, on the last day dingyou, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: ----2十一月，丁卯晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: ----2 In the eleventh month, on the last day dingmao, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In the eleventh month, on the last day dingmao, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: ----3詔曰：「前遣列侯之國，或辭未行。

translations.literal: ----3 An edict said: "Previously I sent the ranked marquises to their states; some declined and have not yet gone.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 An edict said, "I previously sent the ranked marquises to their states; some declined and have not yet departed.

sentences.zh: 丞相，朕之所重，其為朕率列侯之國！

translations.literal: The chancellor is one whom I hold in weight—let him lead the ranked marquises to their states for me!
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor is one I hold in the highest regard—let him lead the ranked marquises to their states for me!

sentences.zh: 」十二月，免丞相勃，遣就國。

translations.literal: " In the twelfth month, the chancellor Bo was dismissed and sent to his state.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twelfth month, Chancellor Bo was dismissed and sent to his state.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以太尉灌嬰為丞相；

translations.literal: On yihai, the Grand Commandant Guan Ying was made chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Grand Commandant Guan Ying was made chancellor;

sentences.zh: 罷太尉官，屬丞相。

translations.literal: the office of Grand Commandant was abolished and subordinated to the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: the office of Grand Commandant was abolished and placed under the chancellor.

sentences.zh: ----4夏，四月，城陽景王章薨。

translations.literal: ----4 In summer, the fourth month, King Jing of Chengyang, Zhang, died.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In summer, the fourth month, King Jing of Chengyang, Zhang, died.

sentences.zh: ----5初，趙王敖獻美人於高祖，得幸，有娠。

translations.literal: ----5 At the outset, King Ao of Zhao presented a beauty to the High Ancestor; she won favor and became pregnant.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 At the outset, King Ao of Zhao presented a beauty to the High Ancestor; she won his favor and became pregnant.

sentences.zh: 及貫高事發，美人亦坐系河內。

translations.literal: When the affair of Guan Gao broke out, the beauty was also implicated and imprisoned in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair of Guan Gao broke out, the beauty was implicated as well and imprisoned in Henei.

sentences.zh: 美人母弟趙兼因辟陽侯審食其言-{呂后}-，呂后妒，弗肯白。

translations.literal: The beauty's younger brother by the same mother, Zhao Jian, spoke through the Marquis of Piyang Shen Yishi to -{呂后}-; the Empress Lü was jealous and would not speak on her behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The beauty's younger brother Zhao Jian spoke through the Marquis of Piyang Shen Yishi to -{呂后}-; the Empress Lü was jealous and would not plead for her.

sentences.zh: 美人已生子，恚，即自殺。

translations.literal: The beauty had already borne a son; in resentment she at once killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: The beauty had already borne a son; in rage she killed herself.

sentences.zh: 吏奉其子詣上，上悔，名之曰長，令-{呂后}-母之，而葬其母真定。

translations.literal: An officer presented the son to the emperor; the emperor regretted it, named him Chang, ordered -{呂后}- to mother him, and buried his mother at Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: An officer brought the son to the emperor; the emperor was filled with regret, named him Chang, had -{呂后}- raise him as mother, and buried his mother at Zhending.

sentences.zh: 後封長為淮南王。

translations.literal: Later Chang was enfeoffed as king of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chang was enfeoffed as king of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 淮南王蚤失母，常附呂后，故孝惠、-{呂后}-時得無患；

translations.literal: The king of Huainan had early lost his mother and constantly attached himself to the Empress Lü; therefore in the time of Emperor Hui and -{呂后}- he was without trouble;
translations.idiomatic: The king of Huainan had lost his mother early and clung to the Empress Lü; therefore under Emperor Hui and -{呂后}- he came to no harm;

sentences.zh: 而常心怨辟陽侯，以為不強爭之於-{呂后}-，使其母恨而死也。

translations.literal: yet he constantly resented the Marquis of Piyang in his heart, holding that he had not strongly contended for him before -{呂后}-, so that his mother died in hatred.
translations.idiomatic: yet he always resented the Marquis of Piyang, believing he had not pressed his case hard enough before -{呂后}-, so that his mother died in bitterness.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，淮南王自以最親，驕蹇，數不奉法；

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, the king of Huainan, deeming himself the closest kin, was arrogant and obstinate and repeatedly failed to obey the law;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, the king of Huainan, deeming himself the closest kin, grew arrogant and obstinate and repeatedly defied the law;

sentences.zh: 上常寬假之。

translations.literal: the emperor constantly showed him leniency.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor constantly indulged him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，入朝，從上入苑囿獵，與上同車，常謂上「大兄」。

translations.literal: This year he came to court, followed the emperor into the park to hunt, rode in the same carriage with him, and constantly called the emperor "Elder Brother."
translations.idiomatic: That year he came to court, followed the emperor into the parklands to hunt, rode in the same carriage with him, and habitually called the emperor "Elder Brother."

sentences.zh: 王有材力，能扛鼎。

translations.literal: The king had strength and could shoulder a cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: The king was powerfully built and could shoulder a cauldron.

sentences.zh: 乃往見辟陽侯，自袖鐵椎椎辟陽侯，令從者魏敬剄之；

translations.literal: He then went to see the Marquis of Piyang, drew an iron mallet from his sleeve and struck the Marquis of Piyang, and ordered his follower Wei Jing to cut off his head;
translations.idiomatic: He then went to see the Marquis of Piyang, drew an iron mallet from his sleeve and struck him down, and ordered his follower Wei Jing to cut off his head;

sentences.zh: 馳走闕下，肉袒謝罪。

translations.literal: he galloped to the palace gate, bared his torso, and begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: he galloped to the palace gate, bared his torso, and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 帝傷其志為親，故赦弗治。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved by his intent on behalf of kin and therefore pardoned him without prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved by his devotion to kin and pardoned him without prosecution.

sentences.zh: 當是時，薄太后及太子、諸大臣皆憚淮南王。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Bo, the crown prince, and all the great ministers feared the king of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Empress Dowager Bo, the crown prince, and all the great ministers feared the king of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 淮南王以此，歸國益驕恣，出入稱警蹕，稱制擬於天子。

translations.literal: The king of Huainan for this reason, on returning to his state, grew all the more arrogant and unrestrained; going out and coming in he proclaimed imperial escort and styled his commands like the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, on returning to his state the king of Huainan grew all the more arrogant and unrestrained; when he went abroad he proclaimed imperial escort and styled his commands like the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 袁盎諫曰：「諸侯太驕，必生患。

translations.literal: Yuan Ang remonstrated, saying: "If the feudal lords are too arrogant, trouble will surely arise.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ang remonstrated, "If the feudal lords grow too arrogant, trouble will surely follow.

sentences.zh: 」上不聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor did not heed him.

sentences.zh: ----6五月，匈奴右賢王入居河南地，侵盜上郡保塞蠻夷，殺略人民。

translations.literal: ----6 In the fifth month, the Xiongnu Right Worthy King entered and occupied the lands south of the river, raided and plundered the fortified passes of Shang commandery and the frontier barbarians, and killed and carried off the people.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 In the fifth month, the Xiongnu Right Worthy King crossed into the lands south of the river, raided the fortified passes of Shang commandery and the frontier tribes, and killed and carried off the people.

sentences.zh: 上幸甘泉。

translations.literal: The emperor visited Ganquan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to Ganquan.

sentences.zh: 遣丞相灌嬰發車騎八萬五千，詣高奴擊右賢王；

translations.literal: He sent the chancellor Guan Ying to mobilize eighty-five thousand chariots and horsemen to proceed to Gaonu and strike the Right Worthy King;
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chancellor Guan Ying to mobilize eighty-five thousand chariots and horsemen to Gaonu to strike the Right Worthy King;

sentences.zh: 發中尉材官屬衛將軍，軍長安。

translations.literal: he mobilized the skilled soldiers under the commandant of the center to serve the Defender-General and garrison Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: he mobilized the commandant of the center's skilled soldiers under the Defender-General to garrison Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 右賢王走出塞。

translations.literal: The Right Worthy King fled beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Worthy King fled beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: ----7上自甘泉之高奴，因幸太原，見故群臣，皆賜之；

translations.literal: ----7 The emperor, from Ganquan to Gaonu, then visited Taiyuan, saw his former ministers, and all were rewarded;
translations.idiomatic: ----7 The emperor, traveling from Ganquan to Gaonu, then visited Taiyuan, saw his former ministers, and rewarded them all;

sentences.zh: 復晉陽、中都民三歲租。

translations.literal: he remitted three years' rent for the people of Jinyang and Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: he remitted three years' rent for the people of Jinyang and Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 留游太原十餘日。

translations.literal: He lingered and toured Taiyuan for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: He lingered in Taiyuan for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: ----8初，大臣之誅諸呂也，朱虛侯功尤大。

translations.literal: ----8 At the outset, when the great ministers executed the various Lü, the merit of the Marquis of Zhuwei was especially great.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 At the outset, when the great ministers destroyed the Lü clan, the Marquis of Zhuwei's merit was especially great.

sentences.zh: 大臣許盡以趙地王朱虛侯，盡以梁地王東牟侯。

translations.literal: The great ministers had promised to make the Marquis of Zhuwei king of Zhao in full and the Marquis of Dongmou king of Liang in full.
translations.idiomatic: The great ministers had promised to make the Marquis of Zhuwei king of Zhao in full and the Marquis of Dongmou king of Liang in full.

sentences.zh: 及帝立，聞朱虛、東牟之初欲立齊王，故絀其功，及王諸子，乃割齊二郡以王之。

translations.literal: When the emperor was installed, hearing that Zhuwei and Dongmou at first had wished to install the king of Qi, he therefore reduced their merit; when he enfeoffed his sons as kings, he only carved off two commanderies of Qi to make them kings.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was installed, learning that Zhuwei and Dongmou had at first wished to install the king of Qi, he reduced their rewards; when he enfeoffed his sons as kings, he carved off only two commanderies of Qi for them.

sentences.zh: 興居自以失職奪功，頗怏怏；

translations.literal: Xingju himself held that he had lost his post and been robbed of merit and was quite discontent;
translations.idiomatic: Xingju felt he had lost his post and been robbed of his due reward, and was deeply discontent;

sentences.zh: 聞帝幸太原，以為天子且自擊胡，遂發兵反。

translations.literal: hearing that the emperor was visiting Taiyuan, he supposed the Son of Heaven was about to strike the barbarians himself, and therefore raised troops in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: hearing that the emperor was visiting Taiyuan, he supposed the Son of Heaven was about to strike the barbarians in person, and raised troops in revolt.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，罷丞相及行兵皆歸長安，以棘浦侯柴武為大將軍，將四將軍、十萬眾擊之；

translations.literal: When the emperor heard it, he dismissed the chancellor and recalled the marching troops to Chang'an, made the Marquis of Jipo Chai Wu grand general, and led four generals and a hundred thousand men to strike him;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard it, he recalled the chancellor and all marching troops to Chang'an, made the Marquis of Jipo Chai Wu grand general, and sent four generals with a hundred thousand men against him;

sentences.zh: 祁侯繒賀為將軍，軍滎陽。

translations.literal: the Marquis of Qi He was made general and encamped at Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: the Marquis of Qi He was made general and encamped at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，上自太原至長安。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the emperor came from Taiyuan to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the emperor returned from Taiyuan to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 詔：「濟北吏民，兵未至先自定及以軍城邑降者，皆赦之，復官爵；

translations.literal: An edict: "The officials and people of Jibei who before the army arrived had already settled themselves of their own accord or surrendered cities and towns with their forces—all are pardoned and restored in office and rank;
translations.idiomatic: An edict: "The officials and people of Jibei who before the army arrived had already settled matters themselves or surrendered cities and towns—all are pardoned and restored in office and rank;

sentences.zh: 與王興居去來者，赦之。

translations.literal: those who went and came with King Xingju are pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: those who went and came with King Xingju are pardoned."

sentences.zh: 」八月，濟北王興居兵敗，自殺。

translations.literal: " In the eighth month, King Xingju of Jibei's troops were defeated and he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eighth month, King Xingju of Jibei's troops were defeated and he killed himself.

sentences.zh: ----9初，南陽張釋之為騎郎，十年不得調，欲免歸。

translations.literal: ----9 At the outset, Zhang Shizhi of Nanyang served as a cavalry gentleman of the palace; ten years without promotion, he wished to resign and return home.
translations.idiomatic: ----9 At the outset, Zhang Shizhi of Nanyang served as a cavalry gentleman of the palace; after ten years without promotion he wished to resign and go home.

sentences.zh: 袁盎知其賢而薦之，為謁者僕射。

translations.literal: Yuan Ang knew his worth and recommended him; he was made usher and master of attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ang knew his worth and recommended him; he was made usher and master of attendants.

sentences.zh: 釋之從行，登虎圈，上問上林尉諸禽獸簿。

translations.literal: Shizhi followed on the journey; they ascended the tiger enclosure, and the emperor questioned the superintendent of the Shanglin park on the registers of the various birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi accompanied the journey; they ascended the tiger enclosure, and the emperor questioned the superintendent of the Shanglin park on the registers of birds and beasts.

sentences.zh: 十餘問，尉左右視，盡不能對。

translations.literal: After more than ten questions the superintendent looked left and right; none could he answer.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten questions the superintendent looked about; he could answer none of them.

sentences.zh: 虎圈嗇夫從旁代尉對。

translations.literal: The chief of the tiger enclosure answered from the side in place of the superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: The chief of the tiger enclosure answered from the side in the superintendent's stead.

sentences.zh: 上所問禽獸簿甚悉，欲以觀其能；

translations.literal: What the emperor asked about the registers of birds and beasts was very thorough; he wished thereby to observe his ability;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's questions on the registers were very thorough; he wished to test the man's ability;

sentences.zh: 口對響應，無窮者。

translations.literal: he answered by mouth in echoing response, without end.
translations.idiomatic: the man answered fluently, without end.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吏不當若是邪！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Should an officer not be like this!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Should an officer not be like this!

sentences.zh: 尉無賴！

translations.literal: The superintendent is worthless!
translations.idiomatic: The superintendent is worthless!

sentences.zh: 」乃詔釋之拜嗇夫為上林令。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Shizhi to invest the chief as superintendent of Shanglin.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered Shizhi to invest the chief as superintendent of Shanglin.

sentences.zh: 釋之久之前，曰：「陛下以絳侯周勃何如人也？

translations.literal: Shizhi advanced and stood long before him, saying: "Your Majesty, what sort of man do you hold the Marquis of Jiang Zhou Bo to be?
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty, what sort of man do you hold the Marquis of Jiang Zhou Bo to be?

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「長者也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "A man of worth.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "A man of worth.

sentences.zh: 」又復問：「東陽侯張相如何如人也？

translations.literal: " He again asked: "What sort of man is the Marquis of Dongyang Zhang Xiang?
translations.idiomatic: " He asked again, "What sort of man is the Marquis of Dongyang Zhang Xiang?

sentences.zh: 」上復曰：「長者。

translations.literal: " The emperor again said: "A man of worth.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor again said, "A man of worth.

sentences.zh: 」釋之曰：「夫絳侯、東陽侯稱為長者，此兩人言事曾不能出口，豈效此嗇夫喋喋利口捷給哉！

translations.literal: " Shizhi said: "The Marquis of Jiang and the Marquis of Dongyang are called men of worth—yet these two men, when speaking of affairs, could not get a word out; how could one imitate this chief's clattering, sharp-tongued quick replies!
translations.idiomatic: " Shizhi said, "The Marquis of Jiang and the Marquis of Dongyang are called men of worth—yet these two could scarcely get a word out when speaking of affairs. How could one imitate this chief's clattering, sharp-tongued quick replies!

sentences.zh: 且秦以任刀筆之吏，爭以亟疾苛察相高。

translations.literal: Moreover Qin employed clerks with knife and brush; they vied to set one another high in haste, severity, and minute scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Qin put its trust in clerks with knife and brush; they vied to outdo one another in haste, severity, and petty scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 其敝，徒文具而無實，不聞其過，陵遲至於土崩。

translations.literal: Its harm was that there was only paper show without substance, faults went unheard, and decline dragged on until the realm collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The harm was empty paperwork without substance, faults went unheard, and decline dragged on until the realm collapsed.

sentences.zh: 今陛下以嗇夫口辨而超遷之，臣恐天下隨風而靡，爭為口辨而無其實。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty would promote this chief for glib speech—I fear all under Heaven would follow the wind and strive for glib speech without substance.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty would promote this chief for glib speech—I fear the realm would follow the wind and strive for glib speech without substance.

sentences.zh: 夫下之化上，疾於景響，舉錯不可不審也。

translations.literal: How the lower transforms to the upper is swifter than shadow to sound; what is raised and set down cannot go unexamined."
translations.idiomatic: How the lower transforms to match the upper is swifter than shadow to echo; what you raise and set down cannot go unexamined."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「善！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Well said!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Well said!

sentences.zh: 」乃不拜嗇夫。

translations.literal: " He then did not invest the chief.
translations.idiomatic: " He then did not invest the chief.

sentences.zh: 上就車，詔釋之參乘。

translations.literal: The emperor mounted his carriage and ordered Shizhi to ride beside him as attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mounted his carriage and ordered Shizhi to ride beside him as attendant.

sentences.zh: 徐行，問釋之秦之敝，具以質言。

translations.literal: They went slowly, and the emperor asked Shizhi about Qin's harms; he set them forth in full with plain truth.
translations.idiomatic: They went slowly, and the emperor asked Shizhi about Qin's harms; he laid them out plainly and in full.

sentences.zh: 至宮，上拜釋之為公車令。

translations.literal: On reaching the palace, the emperor invested Shizhi as master of the imperial carriages.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the palace, the emperor made Shizhi master of the imperial carriages.

sentences.zh: 頃之，太子與梁王共車入朝，不下司馬門。

translations.literal: Before long the crown prince and the king of Liang entered court in the same carriage and did not dismount at the Gate of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the crown prince and the king of Liang entered court in the same carriage and did not dismount at the Gate of the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 於是釋之追止太子、梁王，無得入殿門，遂劾「不下公門，不敬」，奏之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shizhi pursued and halted the crown prince and the king of Liang; they might not enter the hall gate; he then impeached them for "not dismounting at the public gate—indecorum" and memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Shizhi pursued and halted the crown prince and the king of Liang; they might not enter the hall gate; he impeached them for "not dismounting at the public gate—indecorum" and memorialized it.

sentences.zh: 薄太后聞之；

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Bo heard of it;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Bo heard of it;

sentences.zh: 帝免冠，謝教兒子不謹。

translations.literal: the emperor removed his cap and apologized for not having taught his sons with care.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor removed his cap and apologized for not having taught his sons with sufficient care.

sentences.zh: 薄太后乃使使承詔赦太子、梁王，然後得入。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Bo then sent an envoy bearing the edict to pardon the crown prince and the king of Liang; only then might they enter.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Bo then sent an envoy bearing the edict to pardon the crown prince and the king of Liang; only then could they enter.

sentences.zh: 帝由是奇釋之，拜為中大夫；

translations.literal: The emperor for this reason marveled at Shizhi and invested him as palace grandee;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor for this reason marveled at Shizhi and made him palace grandee;

sentences.zh: 頃之，至中郎將。

translations.literal: before long he rose to commandant of the palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: before long he rose to commandant of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 從行至霸陵，上謂群臣曰：「嗟乎！

translations.literal: Following on the journey to Baling, the emperor said to the ministers: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: On the journey to Baling, the emperor said to the ministers, "Alas!

sentences.zh: 以北山石為槨，用紵絮昔斮陳漆其間，豈可動哉！

translations.literal: to take northern mountain stone for the outer coffin, use ramie floss and old hemp to pack and lay lacquer within—could it be moved!
translations.idiomatic: to take stone from the northern mountains for the outer coffin, pack it with ramie floss and old hemp and lay lacquer within—who could breach it!

sentences.zh: 」左右皆曰：「善！

translations.literal: " Those beside him all said: "Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: " Those beside him all said, "Excellent!

sentences.zh: 」釋之曰：「使其中有可欲者，雖錮南山猶有隙；

translations.literal: " Shizhi said: "If within there is something to be desired, though the southern mountains were caged there would still be a gap;
translations.idiomatic: " Shizhi said, "If within there is something to be desired, though you caged the southern mountains there would still be a gap;

sentences.zh: 使其中無可欲者，雖無石槨，又何戚焉！

translations.literal: if within there is nothing to be desired, though there were no stone coffin, what sorrow would there be!"
translations.idiomatic: if within there is nothing to be desired, though there were no stone coffin, what would there be to grieve over!"

sentences.zh: 」帝稱善。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised it as well said.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor praised it as well said.

translations.idiomatic: for this reason without levies the state's expenditure was ample.

sentences.zh: 於是吳、鄧錢布天下。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wu and Deng coins spread through all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wu and Deng coins spread through all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: ----3初，帝分代為二國，立皇子武為代王，參為太原王。

translations.literal: ----3 At first the Emperor divided Dai into two states, installing his son Wu as king of Dai and Can as king of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 At first the Emperor divided Dai into two states, installing his son Wu as king of Dai and Can as king of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 是歲，徙代王武為淮陽王；

translations.literal: This year the king of Dai Wu was moved to be king of Huaiyang;
translations.idiomatic: This year the king of Dai Wu was moved to be king of Huaiyang;

sentences.zh: 以太原王參為代王，盡得故地。

translations.literal: the king of Taiyuan Can was made king of Dai and fully received the former territory.
translations.idiomatic: the king of Taiyuan Can was made king of Dai and fully received the former territory.

sentences.zh: ----1冬，十月，桃、李華。

translations.literal: ----1 In winter, the tenth month, peach and plum blossomed.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In winter, the tenth month, peach and plum blossomed.

sentences.zh: ----2淮南厲王長自作法令行於其國，逐漢所置吏，請自置相、二千石；

translations.literal: ----2 King Li of Huainan Liu Chang himself made laws and executed them in his state, expelled Han-appointed officials, and requested to appoint his own chancellor and officials at two thousand dan;
translations.idiomatic: ----2 King Li of Huainan Liu Chang himself made laws and executed them in his state, expelled Han-appointed officials, and requested to appoint his own chancellor and officials at two thousand dan;

sentences.zh: 帝曲意從之。

translations.literal: the Emperor bent his intent and assented.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor bent his intent and assented.

sentences.zh: 又擅刑殺不辜及爵人至關內侯；

translations.literal: He also on his own authority punished and killed the innocent and ennobled men up to marquis within the passes;
translations.idiomatic: He also on his own authority punished and killed the innocent and ennobled men up to marquis within the passes;

sentences.zh: 數上書不遜順。

translations.literal: repeatedly submitted memorials that were not deferential and compliant.
translations.idiomatic: repeatedly submitted memorials that were not deferential and compliant.

sentences.zh: 帝重自切責之，乃令薄昭與書風諭之，引管、蔡及代頃王、濟北王興居以為儆戒。

translations.literal: The Emperor heavily reproached himself and then ordered Bo Zhao to write a letter admonishing him, citing Guan and Cai and the kings of Dai Qing, Jibei, and Xingju as warnings.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor heavily reproached him and then ordered Bo Zhao to write a letter admonishing him, citing Guan and Cai and the kings of Dai Qing, Jibei, and Xingju as warnings.

sentences.zh: 王不說，令大夫但、士伍開章等七十人與棘蒲侯柴武太子奇謀以輦車四十乘反谷口；

translations.literal: The king was displeased and ordered the grandee Dan, commoner Kai Zhang, and seventy others together with the heir of the Marquis of Jipu Chai Wu, Qi, to plot with forty chariots of the imperial train to rebel at Gukou;
translations.idiomatic: The king was displeased and ordered the grandee Dan, commoner Kai Zhang, and seventy others together with the heir of the Marquis of Jipu Chai Wu, Qi, to plot with forty chariots of the imperial train to rebel at Gukou;

sentences.zh: 令人使閩越、匈奴。

translations.literal: he sent men as envoys to Minyue and the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: he sent men as envoys to Minyue and the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 事覺，有司治之。

translations.literal: The affair was discovered and the relevant offices tried it.
translations.idiomatic: The affair was discovered and the relevant offices tried it.

sentences.zh: 使使召淮南王。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent to summon the king of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to summon the king of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 王至長安，丞相張蒼、典客馮敬行御史大夫事，與宗正、廷尉奏：「長罪當棄市。

translations.literal: When the king reached Chang'an, Chancellor Zhang Cang and the Director of Guests Feng Jing acting as Grandee Secretary, together with the Director of the Imperial Clan and the Commandant of Justice, memorialized: "Chang's crime warrants exposure in the market.
translations.idiomatic: When the king reached Chang'an, Chancellor Zhang Cang and the Director of Guests Feng Jing acting as Grandee Secretary, together with the Director of the Imperial Clan and the Commandant of Justice, memorialized, "Chang's crime warrants exposure in the market."

sentences.zh: 」制曰：「其赦長死罪，廢，勿王；

translations.literal: " The rescript said: "Pardon Chang's capital crime; depose him—do not let him remain king;
translations.idiomatic: " The rescript said, "Pardon Chang's capital crime; depose him—do not let him remain king;

sentences.zh: 徙處蜀郡嚴道邛郵。

translations.literal: banish him to Qiongdu in Yandao of Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: banish him to Qiongdu in Yandao of Shu commandery."

sentences.zh: 」盡誅所與謀者。

translations.literal: " All who plotted with him were executed.
translations.idiomatic: " All who plotted with him were executed.

sentences.zh: 載長以輜車，令縣以次傳之。

translations.literal: Chang was carried in a supply cart; counties were ordered to relay him in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was carried in a supply cart; counties were ordered to relay him in sequence.

sentences.zh: 袁盎諫曰：「上素驕淮南王，弗為置嚴傅、相，以故至此。

translations.literal: Yuan Ang remonstrated, saying: "Your Majesty has always indulged the king of Huainan and did not appoint a strict tutor and chancellor; for this reason it has come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ang remonstrated, saying, "Your Majesty has always indulged the king of Huainan and did not appoint a strict tutor and chancellor; for this reason it has come to this.

sentences.zh: 淮南王為人剛，今暴摧折之，臣恐卒逢霧露病死，陛下有殺弟之名，奈何？

translations.literal: The king of Huainan is by nature stern; now if he is suddenly broken and bent, your servant fears he may in the end meet mist and dew and die of illness—Your Majesty would have the name of killing a younger brother; what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: The king of Huainan is by nature stern; now if he is suddenly broken and bent, I fear he may in the end meet mist and dew and die of illness—Your Majesty would have the name of killing a younger brother; what is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「吾特苦之耳，今復之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "I only meant to distress him; now I restore him.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "I only meant to distress him; now I restore him."

sentences.zh: 淮南王果憤恚不食死。

translations.literal: The king of Huainan indeed died of rage and resentment from refusing food.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Huainan indeed died of rage and resentment from refusing food.

sentences.zh: 縣傳至雍，雍令發封，以死聞。

translations.literal: When the relay reached Yong, the magistrate of Yong broke the seal and reported the death.
translations.idiomatic: When the relay reached Yong, the magistrate of Yong broke the seal and reported the death.

sentences.zh: 上哭甚悲，謂袁盎曰：「吾不聽公言，卒亡淮南王！

translations.literal: The Emperor wept very bitterly and said to Yuan Ang: "I did not heed your words and in the end lost the king of Huainan!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wept very bitterly and said to Yuan Ang, "I did not heed your words and in the end lost the king of Huainan!

sentences.zh: 今為奈何？

translations.literal: Now what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Now what is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 」盎曰：「獨斬丞相、御史以謝天下乃可。

translations.literal: " Ang said: "Only by executing the Chancellor and the Censor to apologize to all under Heaven can it be done.
translations.idiomatic: " Ang said, "Only by executing the Chancellor and the Censor to apologize to all under Heaven can it be done."

sentences.zh: 」上即令丞相、御史逮考諸縣傳送淮南王不發封饋侍者，皆棄市；

translations.literal: " The Emperor immediately ordered the Chancellor and Censor to arrest and try all along the relay who transported the king of Huainan without breaking the seal or supplying attendants—all were exposed in the market;
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor immediately ordered the Chancellor and Censor to arrest and try all along the relay who transported the king of Huainan without breaking the seal or supplying attendants—all were exposed in the market;

sentences.zh: 以列侯葬淮南王於雍，置守塚三十戶。

translations.literal: the king of Huainan was buried at Yong with the rites of a full marquis, and thirty households were set to guard the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: the king of Huainan was buried at Yong with the rites of a full marquis, and thirty households were set to guard the tomb.

sentences.zh: ----3匈奴單于遣漢書曰：「前時，皇帝言和親事，稱書意，合歡。

translations.literal: ----3 The Chanyu of the Xiongnu sent a letter to Han, saying: "Previously the Emperor spoke of the marriage-alliance affair; the letter's intent was praised and accorded with joy.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 The Chanyu of the Xiongnu sent a letter to Han, saying, "Previously the Emperor spoke of the marriage-alliance affair; the letter's intent was praised and accorded with joy.

sentences.zh: 漢邊吏侵侮右賢王；

translations.literal: Han frontier officials insulted and humiliated the Right Worthy King;
translations.idiomatic: Han frontier officials insulted and humiliated the Right Worthy King;

sentences.zh: 右賢王不請，聽後義盧侯難支等計，與漢吏相距。

translations.literal: the Right Worthy King did not request permission but heeded the plan of the Rear Yilu Marquis Nazhi and others and opposed Han officials.
translations.idiomatic: the Right Worthy King did not request permission but heeded the plan of the Rear Yilu Marquis Nazhi and others and opposed Han officials.

sentences.zh: 絕二主之約，離兄弟之親，故罰右賢王，使之西求月氏擊之。

translations.literal: He broke the covenant of the two rulers and severed the kinship of brothers; therefore he punished the Wise King of the Right and sent him west to seek the Yuezhi and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: He broke the covenant of the two rulers and severed the bond of brotherhood; therefore he punished the Wise King of the Right and sent him west to seek the Yuezhi and attack them.

sentences.zh: 以天之福，吏卒良，馬力強，以夷滅月氏，盡斬殺、降下，定之；

translations.literal: By Heaven's blessing, officers and soldiers were good and horses' strength strong; he extinguished the Yuezhi as barbarians, beheaded and killed all, made them submit, and settled them;
translations.idiomatic: By Heaven's blessing, officers and soldiers were capable and horses strong; he destroyed the Yuezhi as barbarians, beheaded and killed them all, made them submit, and settled them;

sentences.zh: 樓蘭、烏孫、呼揭及其旁二十六國，皆已為匈奴，諸引弓之民並為一家，北州以定。

translations.literal: Kroraina, Wusun, Hujie, and the twenty-six states beside them all already belonged to the Xiongnu; all bow-drawing peoples became one house, and the northern regions were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Kroraina, Wusun, Hujie, and the twenty-six states beside them all already belonged to the Xiongnu; all bow-drawing peoples became one house, and the northern regions were settled.

sentences.zh: 願寢兵，休士卒，養馬，除前事，復故約，以安邊民。

translations.literal: I wish to lay down arms, rest officers and soldiers, nurture horses, set aside past affairs, restore the former covenant, and thereby settle the border people.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to lay down arms, rest the troops, nurture horses, set aside past affairs, restore the former covenant, and thereby settle the border people.

sentences.zh: 皇帝即不欲匈奴近塞，則且詔吏民遠舍。

translations.literal: If the Emperor does not wish the Xiongnu near the passes, then for the time being let him decree that officials and people move their dwellings far off.
translations.idiomatic: If the Emperor does not wish the Xiongnu near the passes, then for the time being let him decree that officials and people move their dwellings far off.

sentences.zh: 」帝報書曰：「單于欲除前事，復故約，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor replied in a letter, saying: "The Chanyu wishes to set aside past affairs and restore the former covenant—I greatly commend this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor replied in a letter: "The Chanyu wishes to set aside past affairs and restore the former covenant—I greatly commend this.

sentences.zh: 此古聖王之志也。

translations.literal: This is the aim of the ancient sage kings.
translations.idiomatic: This is the aim of the ancient sage kings.

sentences.zh: 漢與匈奴約為兄弟，所以遺單于甚厚；

translations.literal: Han and the Xiongnu covenanted as brothers; for this reason what was sent to the Chanyu was very generous;
translations.idiomatic: Han and the Xiongnu covenanted as brothers; for this reason what was sent to the Chanyu was very generous;

sentences.zh: 倍約、離兄弟之親者，常在匈奴。

translations.literal: those who doubled the covenant and severed the kinship of brothers were constantly on the Xiongnu side.
translations.idiomatic: those who broke the covenant and severed the bond of brotherhood were constantly on the Xiongnu side.

sentences.zh: 然右賢王事已在赦前，單于勿深誅！

translations.literal: Yet the Wise King of the Right's affair was already before the amnesty—the Chanyu must not punish him deeply!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Wise King of the Right's affair was already before the amnesty—the Chanyu must not punish him severely!

sentences.zh: 單于若稱書意，明告諸吏，使無負約，有信，敬如單于書。

translations.literal: If the Chanyu accords with the letter's intent, let him clearly tell all his officers to not betray the covenant, to have good faith—[we] will respect it as the Chanyu's letter.
translations.idiomatic: If the Chanyu accords with the letter's intent, let him clearly tell all his officers not to betray the covenant and to keep faith—we will respect it as the Chanyu's letter.

sentences.zh: 後頃之，冒頓死，子稽粥立，號曰老上單于。

translations.literal: After a short while Modun died; his son Jizhou was established, styled Laoshang Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: After a short while Modun died; his son Jizhou was established, styled Laoshang Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 老上單于初立，帝復遣宗室女翁主為單于閼氏，使宦者燕人中行說傅翁主。

translations.literal: When Laoshang Chanyu had just been established, the Emperor again sent a clanswoman, the Lady Wengzhu, to be the Chanyu's consort, and appointed the eunuch Yan man Zhonghang Yue to tutor the Lady Wengzhu.
translations.idiomatic: When Laoshang Chanyu had just been established, the Emperor again sent a clanswoman, the Lady Wengzhu, to be the Chanyu's consort, and appointed the eunuch Yan man Zhonghang Yue to tutor the Lady Wengzhu.

sentences.zh: 說不欲行，漢強使之。

translations.literal: Yue did not wish to go; Han forced him to go.
translations.idiomatic: Yue did not wish to go; Han forced him to go.

sentences.zh: 說曰：「必我也，為漢患者！

translations.literal: Yue said: "It must be I who will bring harm upon Han!
translations.idiomatic: Yue said: "It must be I who will bring harm upon Han!"

sentences.zh: 」中行說既至，因降單于，單于甚親幸之。

translations.literal: " When Zhonghang Yue had arrived, he thereupon defected to the Chanyu; the Chanyu was very intimate and favored toward him.
translations.idiomatic: " When Zhonghang Yue had arrived, he thereupon defected to the Chanyu; the Chanyu was very intimate with him and greatly favored him.

sentences.zh: 初，匈奴好漢繒絮、食物。

translations.literal: At first the Xiongnu loved Han silk floss and foodstuffs.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Xiongnu loved Han silk floss and foodstuffs.

sentences.zh: 中行說曰：「匈奴人眾不能當漢之一郡，然所以強者，以衣食異，無仰於漢也。

translations.literal: Zhonghang Yue said: "The Xiongnu in population cannot match a single Han commandery, yet the reason they are strong is that clothing and food differ and they have no dependence on Han.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghang Yue said: "The Xiongnu in population cannot match a single Han commandery, yet the reason they are strong is that clothing and food differ and they have no dependence on Han.

sentences.zh: 今單于變俗，好漢物；

translations.literal: Now the Chanyu changes custom and loves Han goods;
translations.idiomatic: Now the Chanyu changes custom and loves Han goods;

sentences.zh: 漢物不過什二，則匈奴盡歸於漢矣。

translations.literal: if Han goods do not exceed two-tenths, then the Xiongnu will all belong to Han.
translations.idiomatic: if Han goods do not exceed two-tenths, then the Xiongnu will all belong to Han.

sentences.zh: 」其得漢繒絮，以馳草棘中，衣胯皆裂敝，以示不如旃裘之完善也；

translations.literal: " When they obtained Han silk floss, they galloped through grass and brambles with it; the clothing at the hips all split and wore out, to show it was not as complete as felt and fur robes;
translations.idiomatic: " When they obtained Han silk floss, they galloped through grass and brambles with it; the clothing at the hips all split and wore out, to show it was not as durable as felt and fur robes;

sentences.zh: 得漢食物，皆去之，以示不如湩酪之便美也。

translations.literal: when they obtained Han foodstuffs, they all discarded them, to show they were not as convenient and fine as fermented mare's milk.
translations.idiomatic: when they obtained Han foodstuffs, they all discarded them, to show they were not as convenient and fine as fermented mare's milk.

sentences.zh: 於是說教單于左右疏記，以計課其人眾、畜牧。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yue taught the Chanyu's attendants to keep written tallies and, by reckoning, assess their population and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yue taught the Chanyu's attendants to keep written tallies and, by reckoning, assess their population and livestock.

sentences.zh: 其遺漢書牘及印封，皆令長大，倨傲其辭，自稱「天地所生、日月所置匈奴大單于」。

translations.literal: When they sent letters and documents to Han and sealed them with the seal, he had them all made large, haughty in wording, styling himself "Great Chanyu of the Xiongnu, begotten by Heaven and Earth, established by sun and moon."
translations.idiomatic: When they sent letters and documents to Han and sealed them with the seal, he had them all made large, haughty in wording, styling himself "Great Chanyu of the Xiongnu, begotten by Heaven and Earth, established by sun and moon."

sentences.zh: 漢使或訾笑匈奴俗無禮義者，中行說輒窮漢使曰：「匈奴約束徑，易行；

translations.literal: When Han envoys sometimes reviled and laughed at Xiongnu custom for lacking ritual and righteousness, Zhonghang Yue would press the Han envoys hard, saying: "Xiongnu regulations are direct and easy to carry out;
translations.idiomatic: When Han envoys sometimes reviled and laughed at Xiongnu custom for lacking ritual and righteousness, Zhonghang Yue would press the Han envoys hard: "Xiongnu regulations are direct and easy to carry out;

sentences.zh: 君臣簡，可久；

translations.literal: lord and minister are simple and can long endure;
translations.idiomatic: lord and minister are simple and can long endure;

sentences.zh: 一國之政，猶一體也。

translations.literal: a state's government is like one body.
translations.idiomatic: a state's government is like one body.

sentences.zh: 故匈奴雖亂，必立宗種。

translations.literal: Therefore though the Xiongnu are in disorder, they are sure to establish the lineage seed.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore though the Xiongnu are in disorder, they are sure to establish the lineage heir.

sentences.zh: 今中國雖-{云}-有禮義，及親屬益疏則相殺奪，以至易姓，皆從此類也。

translations.literal: Now China, though it has -{云}- ritual and righteousness, when kin grow ever more distant they kill and seize from one another, even to the point of changing the surname—all from this sort of thing.
translations.idiomatic: Now China, though it has -{云}- ritual and righteousness, when kin grow ever more distant they kill and seize from one another, even to the point of changing the surname—all from this sort of thing.

sentences.zh: 嗟！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 土室之人，顧無多辭，喋喋占占！

translations.literal: Men of earthen chambers—why so much talk, chattering and prognosticating!
translations.idiomatic: Men of earthen chambers—why so much talk, chattering and prognosticating!

sentences.zh: 顧漢所輸匈奴繒絮、米薛，令其量中，必善美而已矣，何以言為乎！

translations.literal: Simply see that what Han sends the Xiongnu in silk floss and grain is measured full and must be good and fine—that is enough; what need is there for words!
translations.idiomatic: Simply see that what Han sends the Xiongnu in silk floss and grain is measured full and must be good and fine—that is enough; what need is there for words!

sentences.zh: 且所給，備、善，則已；

translations.literal: Moreover, what is given—if complete and good, then that is enough;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, what is given—if complete and good, then that is enough;

sentences.zh: 不備、苦惡，則候秋熟，以騎馳蹂而稼穡耳！

translations.literal: if not complete and bitterly bad, then wait until the autumn ripening and with cavalry gallop and trample the crops!
translations.idiomatic: if not complete and bitterly bad, then wait until the autumn ripening and with cavalry gallop and trample the crops!

sentences.zh: 」----4梁太傅賈誼上疏曰：

translations.literal: " ----4 Grand Tutor of Liang Jia Yi submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: " ----4 Grand Tutor of Liang Jia Yi submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: :「臣竊惟今之事勢，可為痛哭者一，可為流涕者二，可為長太息者六；

translations.literal: :"Your servant privately considers the present situation: there is one matter for which one may weep bitterly, two for which one may shed tears, and six for which one may sigh long;
translations.idiomatic: :"Your servant privately considers the present situation: there is one matter for which one may weep bitterly, two for which one may shed tears, and six for which one may sigh long;

sentences.zh: 若其它背理而傷道者，難遍以疏舉。

translations.literal: as for other matters contrary to principle and injurious to the Way, it is hard to enumerate them all in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: as for other matters contrary to principle and injurious to the Way, it is hard to enumerate them all in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 進言者皆曰：『天下已安已治矣，』臣獨以為未也。

translations.literal: Those who advance counsel all say: 'All under Heaven is already secure and already well governed,' but your servant alone considers that it is not yet so.
translations.idiomatic: Those who advance counsel all say: 'The realm is already secure and already well governed,' but your servant alone considers that it is not yet so.

sentences.zh: 曰安且治者，非愚則諛，皆非事實知治亂之體者也。

translations.literal: Those who say it is secure and well governed are either foolish or flatterers; none truly know the substance of order and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Those who say it is secure and well governed are either foolish or flatterers; none truly know the substance of order and disorder.

sentences.zh: 夫抱火厝之積薪之下而寢其上，火未及然，因謂之安；

translations.literal: To hold fire and place it under a pile of kindling yet sleep atop it—before the fire has reached the point of blazing, one therefore calls it secure;
translations.idiomatic: To hold fire and place it under a pile of kindling yet sleep atop it—before the fire has reached the point of blazing, one therefore calls it secure;

sentences.zh: 方今之勢，何以異此！

translations.literal: the present situation—how does it differ from this!
translations.idiomatic: the present situation—how does it differ from this!

sentences.zh: 陛下何不壹令臣得孰數之於前，因陳治安之策，試詳擇焉！

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty not at once let your servant enumerate them in detail before you and, thereby presenting policies for securing order, try to choose carefully among them!
translations.idiomatic: Why does Your Majesty not at once let your servant enumerate them in detail before you and, thereby presenting policies for securing order, try to choose carefully among them!

sentences.zh: :使為治，勞智慮，苦身體，乏鐘、鼓之樂，勿為可也。

translations.literal: :To govern may weary the mind's deliberation and distress the body, and lack the pleasure of bells and drums—that may be done.
translations.idiomatic: :To govern may weary the mind's deliberation and distress the body, and lack the pleasure of bells and drums—that may be done.

sentences.zh: 樂與今同，而加之諸侯軌道，兵革不動，匈奴賓服，百姓素樸，生為明帝，沒為明神，名譽之美垂於無窮，使顧成之廟稱為太宗，上配太祖，與漢亡極，立經陳紀，為萬世法。

translations.literal: If pleasure is the same as today, yet in addition the feudal lords keep to the track, arms and armor are not moved, the Xiongnu guest and submit, the hundred surnames are plain and simple, living as a Brilliant Emperor and dying as a Brilliant Spirit, the beauty of fame extending without end, causing the temple of Gu Cheng to be styled Taizong, matching above with Taizu, with Han without end, establishing classics and setting forth ordinances as law for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: If pleasure is the same as today, yet in addition the feudal lords keep to the track, arms and armor are not moved, the Xiongnu guest and submit, the common people are plain and simple, living as a Brilliant Emperor and dying as a Brilliant Spirit, the beauty of fame extending without end, causing the temple of Gu Cheng to be styled Taizong, matching above with Taizu, with Han without end, establishing classics and setting forth ordinances as law for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 雖有愚幼、不肖之嗣，猶得蒙業而安。

translations.literal: Even if there were a foolish young or unworthy heir, he would still obtain the inherited enterprise and be secure.
translations.idiomatic: Even if there were a foolish young or unworthy heir, he would still obtain the inherited enterprise and be secure.

sentences.zh: 以陛下之明達，因使少知治體者得佐下風，致此非難也。

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's brilliance and penetration, thereby letting those who slightly know the substance of governance assist below your wind—to achieve this is not difficult.
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's brilliance and penetration, thereby letting those who slightly know the substance of governance assist below your wind—to achieve this is not difficult.

sentences.zh: :夫樹國固必相疑之勢，下數被其殃，上數爽其憂，甚非所以安上而全下也。

translations.literal: :To plant states is inherently a situation of mutual suspicion; those below repeatedly suffer their calamities, those above repeatedly miss their worries—this is very far from securing the superior and preserving the inferior.
translations.idiomatic: :To plant states is inherently a situation of mutual suspicion; those below repeatedly suffer their calamities, those above repeatedly miss their worries—this is very far from securing the superior and preserving the inferior.

sentences.zh: 今或親弟謀為東帝，親兄之子西鄉而擊，今吳又見告矣。

translations.literal: Now perhaps a full younger brother plots to be Eastern Emperor, a full elder brother's son turns west and attacks, and now Wu has again been reported.
translations.idiomatic: Now perhaps a full younger brother plots to be Eastern Emperor, a full elder brother's son turns west and attacks, and now Wu has again been reported.

sentences.zh: 天子春秋鼎盛，行義未過，德澤有加焉，猶尚如是；

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven is in the prime of life, his conduct and righteousness not yet in error, his virtue and grace still increasing—yet it is still like this;
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven is in the prime of life, his conduct and righteousness not yet in error, his virtue and grace still increasing—yet it is still like this;

sentences.zh: 況莫大諸侯，權力且十此者虖！

translations.literal: how much more when great feudal lords have power nearly ten times this!
translations.idiomatic: how much more when great feudal lords have power nearly ten times this!

sentences.zh: :然而天下少安，何也？

translations.literal: :Yet all under Heaven is slightly secure—why?
translations.idiomatic: :Yet the realm is slightly secure—why?

sentences.zh: 大國之王幼弱未壯，漢之所置傅、相方握其事。

translations.literal: The kings of great states are young and weak, not yet grown; the tutors and chancellors Han has appointed just now hold their affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The kings of great states are young and weak, not yet grown; the tutors and chancellors Han has appointed just now hold their affairs.

sentences.zh: 數年之後，諸侯之王大抵皆冠，血氣方剛；

translations.literal: After several years, the kings of the feudal lords will for the most part all come of age, blood and vigor just firm;
translations.idiomatic: After several years, the kings of the feudal lords will for the most part all come of age, blood and vigor just firm;

sentences.zh: 漢之傅、相稱病而賜罷，彼自丞、尉以上遍置私人。

translations.literal: Han's tutors and chancellors will plead illness and be dismissed with gifts; they themselves from chancellors and commandants upward will everywhere place their own men.
translations.idiomatic: Han's tutors and chancellors will plead illness and be dismissed with gifts; they themselves from chancellors and commandants upward will everywhere place their own men.

sentences.zh: 如此，有異淮南、濟北之為邪？

translations.literal: Like this, is there any difference from what Huainan and Jibei did?
translations.idiomatic: Like this, is there any difference from what Huainan and Jibei did?

sentences.zh: 此時而欲為治安，雖堯、舜不治。

translations.literal: At this time to wish to secure order—even Yao and Shun could not govern it.
translations.idiomatic: At this time to wish to secure order—even Yao and Shun could not govern it.

sentences.zh: :黃帝曰：『日中必熭，操刀必割！

translations.literal: :The Yellow Emperor said: 'At midday one must singe; holding a knife one must cut!
translations.idiomatic: :The Yellow Emperor said: 'At midday one must singe; holding a knife one must cut!

sentences.zh: 』今令此道順而全安甚易，不肯蚤為，已乃墮骨肉之屬而抗剄之，豈有異秦之季世虖！

translations.literal: ' Now to make this course accordant and wholly secure is very easy; unwilling to act early, only afterward to cast down kin of flesh and bone and resist them with the executioner's blade—is this not the same as the late age of Qin!
translations.idiomatic: ' Now to make this course accordant and wholly secure is very easy; unwilling to act early, only afterward to cast down kin of flesh and bone and resist them with the executioner's blade—is this not the same as the late age of Qin!

sentences.zh: 其異姓負強而動者，漢已幸而勝之矣，又不易其所以然；

translations.literal: Those of different surnames who relied on strength and moved—Han has already fortunately overcome them, yet does not change the reason it was so;
translations.idiomatic: Those of different surnames who relied on strength and moved—Han has already fortunately overcome them, yet does not change the reason it was so;

sentences.zh: 同姓襲是跡而動，既有征矣，其勢盡又復然。

translations.literal: those of the same surname follow these tracks and move—there are already signs; when their power is exhausted it will again be so.
translations.idiomatic: those of the same surname follow these tracks and move—there are already signs; when their power is exhausted it will again be so.

sentences.zh: 殃禍之變，未知所移，明帝處之尚不能以安，後世將如之何！

translations.literal: The shift of calamity and disaster is unknown where it will move; a Brilliant Emperor facing it still cannot thereby be secure—how will later generations do!
translations.idiomatic: The shift of calamity and disaster is unknown where it will move; a Brilliant Emperor facing it still cannot thereby be secure—how will later generations do!

sentences.zh: :臣竊跡前事，大抵強者先反。

translations.literal: :Your servant privately traces former affairs: for the most part the strong rebel first.
translations.idiomatic: :Your servant privately traces former affairs: for the most part the strong rebel first.

sentences.zh: 長沙乃二萬五千戶耳，功少而最完，勢疏而最忠，非獨性異人也，亦形勢然也。

translations.literal: Changsha was only twenty-five thousand households; least in merit yet most complete, most distant in position yet most loyal—not solely because the nature was a different man, but also because the situation was so.
translations.idiomatic: Changsha was only twenty-five thousand households; least in merit yet most complete, most distant in position yet most loyal—not solely because the nature was a different man, but also because the situation was so.

sentences.zh: 曩令樊、酈、絳、灌據數十城而王，今雖以殘亡可也；

translations.literal: If formerly Fan, Li, Jiang, and Guan had held dozens of cities and been kings, now even if reduced and destroyed that would be permissible;
translations.idiomatic: If formerly Fan, Li, Jiang, and Guan had held dozens of cities and been kings, now even if reduced and destroyed that would be permissible;

sentences.zh: 令信、越之倫列為徹侯而居，雖至今存可也。

translations.literal: if Xin, Yue, and their sort were ranked as marquises and dwelt thus, even to the present to remain would be permissible.
translations.idiomatic: if Xin, Yue, and their sort were ranked as marquises and dwelt thus, even to the present to remain would be permissible.

sentences.zh: 然則天下之大計可知已：欲諸王之皆忠附，則莫若令如長沙王；

translations.literal: Then the great plan for all under Heaven can be known: if one wishes all the kings to be loyal and attached, there is nothing like making them like the King of Changsha;
translations.idiomatic: Then the great plan for the realm can be known: if one wishes all the kings to be loyal and attached, there is nothing like making them like the King of Changsha;

sentences.zh: 欲臣子勿菹醢，則莫若令如樊、酈等；

translations.literal: if one wishes ministers and sons not to be minced and salted, there is nothing like making them like Fan, Li, and the rest;
translations.idiomatic: if one wishes ministers and sons not to be minced and salted, there is nothing like making them like Fan, Li, and the rest;

sentences.zh: 欲天下之治安，莫若眾建諸侯而少其力。

translations.literal: if one wishes security and order for all under Heaven, there is nothing like establishing many feudal lords and diminishing their power.
translations.idiomatic: if one wishes security and order for the realm, there is nothing like establishing many feudal lords and diminishing their power.

sentences.zh: 力少則易使以義，國小則亡邪心。

translations.literal: When power is little, they are easily employed by righteousness; when the state is small, perverse hearts perish.
translations.idiomatic: When power is little, they are easily employed by righteousness; when the state is small, perverse hearts perish.

sentences.zh: 令海內之勢，如身之使臂，臂之使指，莫不制從，諸侯之君不敢有異心，輻湊並進而歸命天子。

translations.literal: Make the situation within the seas like the body employing the arm, the arm employing the finger—none not controlled and obedient; the lords of the feudal states dare not have divergent hearts, but like wheel spokes converging advance together and return their mandate to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Make the situation within the seas like the body employing the arm, the arm employing the finger—none not controlled and obedient; the lords of the feudal states dare not have divergent hearts, but like wheel spokes converging advance together and return their mandate to the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 割地定製，令齊、趙、楚各為若干國，使悼惠王、幽王、元王之子孫畢以次各受祖之分地，地盡而止；

translations.literal: Cut territory and fix institutions; let Qi, Zhao, and Chu each become several states; cause the descendants of King Daohui, King You, and King Yuan each in turn to receive their ancestor's allotted territory, stopping when the land is exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: Cut territory and fix institutions; let Qi, Zhao, and Chu each become several states; cause the descendants of King Daohui, King You, and King Yuan each in turn to receive their ancestor's allotted territory, stopping when the land is exhausted;

sentences.zh: 其分地眾而子孫少者，建以為國，空而置之，須其子孫生者舉使君之；

translations.literal: where allotted territory is much yet descendants few, establish it as a state, leave it empty and set it aside, and when descendants are born raise one to lord it;
translations.idiomatic: where allotted territory is much yet descendants few, establish it as a state, leave it empty and set it aside, and when descendants are born raise one to lord it;

sentences.zh: 一寸之地，一人之眾，天子亡所利焉，誠以定治而已。

translations.literal: an inch of land, a single man's multitude—the Son of Heaven has no profit from it; truly it is only to fix governance.
translations.idiomatic: an inch of land, a single man's multitude—the Son of Heaven has no profit from it; truly it is only to fix governance.

sentences.zh: 如此，則臥赤子天下之上而安，植遺腹，朝委裘而天下不亂；

translations.literal: Like this, then lying an infant red atop all under Heaven one is secure, planting a posthumous heir, governing in court with a fur robe draped, yet all under Heaven is not in disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Like this, then lying an infant red atop the realm one is secure, planting a posthumous heir, governing in court with a fur robe draped, yet the realm is not in disorder;

sentences.zh: 當時大治，後世誦聖。

translations.literal: the age then greatly ordered, later generations chanting the sage.
translations.idiomatic: the age then greatly ordered, later generations chanting the sage.

sentences.zh: 陛下誰憚而久不為此！

translations.literal: Your Majesty—whom do you fear that you long do not do this!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty—whom do you fear that you long do not do this!

sentences.zh: :天下之勢方病大瘇，一脛之大幾如要，一指之大幾如股，平居不可屈伸，一二指慉，身慮亡聊。

translations.literal: :The situation of all under Heaven is just now afflicted with a great tumor: one shin nearly as large as the waist, one finger nearly as large as the thigh; in ordinary living one cannot bend or stretch; if one or two fingers are distressed, the body fears it has nothing to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: :The situation of the realm is just now afflicted with a great tumor: one shin nearly as large as the waist, one finger nearly as large as the thigh; in ordinary living one cannot bend or stretch; if one or two fingers are distressed, the body fears it has nothing to rely on.

sentences.zh: 失今不治，必為錮疾，後雖有扁鵲，不能為已。

translations.literal: If one misses treating it now, it will surely become an incurable malady; afterward, though there were a Bian Que, he could not cure it.
translations.idiomatic: If one misses treating it now, it will surely become an incurable malady; afterward, though there were a Bian Que, he could not cure it.

sentences.zh: 病非徒腫也。

translations.literal: The disease is not only swelling.
translations.idiomatic: The disease is not only swelling.

sentences.zh: 又苦蹠盭。

translations.literal: There is also the distress of foot ailments.
translations.idiomatic: There is also the distress of foot ailments.

sentences.zh: 元王之子，帝之從弟也；

translations.literal: The son of King Yuan was the Emperor's younger cousin;
translations.idiomatic: The son of King Yuan was the Emperor's younger cousin;

sentences.zh: 今之王者，從弟之子也。

translations.literal: the present king is the son of a younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: the present king is the son of a younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 惠王之子，親兄子也，今之王者，兄子之子也。

translations.literal: The son of King Hui was a full elder brother's son; the present king is a brother's son's son.
translations.idiomatic: The son of King Hui was a full elder brother's son; the present king is a brother's son's son.

sentences.zh: 親者或亡分地以安天下，疏者或制大權以逼天子，臣故曰非徒病腫也，又苦蹠炙盭。

translations.literal: Among the close, some lack allotted territory yet secure all under Heaven; among the distant, some wield great power to press the Son of Heaven—your servant therefore says it is not only the disease of swelling but also the distress of roasted foot ailments.
translations.idiomatic: Among the close, some lack allotted territory yet secure the realm; among the distant, some wield great power to press the Son of Heaven—your servant therefore says it is not only the disease of swelling but also the distress of roasted foot ailments.

sentences.zh: 可痛哭者，此病是也。

translations.literal: That for which one may weep bitterly—this disease is it.
translations.idiomatic: That for which one may weep bitterly—this disease is it.

sentences.zh: :天下之勢方倒懸。

translations.literal: :The situation of all under Heaven is just now inverted and hung.
translations.idiomatic: :The situation of the realm is just now inverted and hung.

sentences.zh: 凡天子者，天下之首。

translations.literal: In general the Son of Heaven is the head of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In general the Son of Heaven is the head of all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 何也？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 上也。

translations.literal: Because he is above.
translations.idiomatic: Because he is above.

sentences.zh: 蠻夷者，天下之足。

translations.literal: The barbarians are the feet of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians are the feet of all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 何也？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 下也。

translations.literal: Because they are below.
translations.idiomatic: Because they are below.

sentences.zh: 今匈奴嫚侮侵掠，至不敬也；

translations.literal: Now the Xiongnu insult, encroach, and plunder, reaching to lack of respect;
translations.idiomatic: Now the Xiongnu insult, encroach, and plunder, reaching to lack of respect;

sentences.zh: 而漢歲致金絮采繒以奉之。

translations.literal: yet Han year after year sends gold, floss, colored silks, and brocades to serve them.
translations.idiomatic: yet Han year after year sends gold, floss, colored silks, and brocades to serve them.

sentences.zh: 足反居上，首顧居下，倒縣如此，莫之能解，猶為國有人乎？

translations.literal: The feet instead dwell above, the head instead dwells below—inverted and hung like this, none able to resolve it; is there still someone in the state?
translations.idiomatic: The feet instead dwell above, the head instead dwells below—inverted and hung like this, none able to resolve it; is there still someone in the state?

sentences.zh: 可為流涕者此也。

translations.literal: That for which one may shed tears is this.
translations.idiomatic: That for which one may shed tears is this.

sentences.zh: :今不獵猛敵而獵田彘，不搏反寇而搏畜菟，翫玩細娛而不圖大患，德可遠加而直數百里外，威令不伸，可為流涕者此也。

translations.literal: :Now one does not hunt fierce enemies but hunts field pigs; does not grapple with rebellious bandits but grapples with domestic rabbits; indulges in petty amusements and does not plan for great peril; virtue could extend far yet reaches only several hundred li beyond, authority and orders not extended—that for which one may shed tears is this.
translations.idiomatic: :Now one does not hunt fierce enemies but hunts field pigs; does not grapple with rebellious bandits but grapples with domestic rabbits; indulges in petty amusements and does not plan for great peril; virtue could extend far yet reaches only several hundred li beyond, authority and orders not extended—that for which one may shed tears is this.

sentences.zh: :今庶人屋壁得為帝服，倡優下賤得為-{后}-飾；

translations.literal: :Now commoners' house walls may have imperial dress; actors and lowly performers may have -{后}- adornments;
translations.idiomatic: :Now commoners' house walls may have imperial dress; actors and lowly performers may have -{后}- adornments;

sentences.zh: 且帝之身自衣皁綈，而富民牆屋被文繡；

translations.literal: moreover the Emperor's own person wears black coarse silk, while rich men's wall houses are draped with patterned embroidery;
translations.idiomatic: moreover the Emperor's own person wears black coarse silk, while rich men's wall houses are draped with patterned embroidery;

sentences.zh: 天子之-{后}-以緣其領，庶人孽妾以緣其履；

translations.literal: the Son of Heaven's -{后}- uses trim for her collar, while a commoner's concubine uses trim for her shoes;
translations.idiomatic: the Son of Heaven's -{后}- uses trim for her collar, while a commoner's concubine uses trim for her shoes;

sentences.zh: 此臣所謂舛也。

translations.literal: This is what your servant calls perversity.
translations.idiomatic: That is the inversion I mean.

sentences.zh: 夫百人作之不能衣一人，欲天下亡寒，胡可得也；

translations.literal: Now a hundred men make it yet cannot clothe one man—if one desires all under Heaven to have no cold, how can it be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: A hundred laborers may weave enough to dress one wastrel—how then can you hope that no one in the realm will shiver?

sentences.zh: 一人耕之，十人聚而食之，欲天下亡饑，不可得也；

translations.literal: One man plows it, ten men gather and eat it—if one desires all under Heaven to have no hunger, it cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: One farmer tills while ten mouths feast on his harvest—you will never banish famine that way.

sentences.zh: 饑寒切於民之肌膚，欲其亡為奸邪，不可得也。

translations.literal: Hunger and cold cut into the people's skin and flesh—if one desires that they not commit wickedness and deviance, it cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: When hunger and cold bite into the flesh, you cannot expect ordinary folk to stay honest.

sentences.zh: 可為長太息者此也。

translations.literal: What may be long sighed for is this.
translations.idiomatic: This is another of the six causes for a long, bitter sigh.

sentences.zh: :商君遺禮義，棄仁恩，並心於進取；

translations.literal: : Lord Shang cast aside ritual and righteousness, abandoned benevolence and kindness, united hearts on advance and seizure;
translations.idiomatic: : When Lord Shang discarded ritual, benevolence, and every humane restraint in favor of naked ambition,

sentences.zh: 行之二歲，秦俗日敗。

translations.literal: practiced two years, and Qin's customs daily decayed.
translations.idiomatic: within two years the customs of Qin rotted away.

sentences.zh: 故秦人家富子壯則出分，家貧子壯則出贅；

translations.literal: Therefore in Qin, if the family was rich and the son grown, then he went out to divide; if the family was poor and the son grown, then he went out to be a son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Hence in Qin a rich family drove out grown sons to split the estate, while a poor family sent them out as indentured sons-in-law;

sentences.zh: 借父櫌鉏，慮有德色；

translations.literal: Borrowing from the father a hoe, one fears there will be a look of conferred virtue;
translations.idiomatic: a son who borrows his father's hoe expects a scowl of condescending favor in return;

sentences.zh: 母取箕帚，立而誶語；

translations.literal: The mother takes broom and dustpan—standing, they revile with words.
translations.idiomatic: a mother-in-law who lends her broom hears muttered curses before her feet have left the room;

sentences.zh: 抱哺其子，與公並居；

translations.literal: Holding and suckling her child, with the father-in-law she dwells together.
translations.idiomatic: a daughter-in-law nurses her baby while lounging as insolently as her father-in-law;

sentences.zh: 婦姑不相說，則反脣而相稽；

translations.literal: If wife and mother-in-law are not pleased with each other, they turn lips and mutually investigate.
translations.idiomatic: when wife and mother-in-law quarrel, they answer each other with sneers and spiteful jibes;

sentences.zh: 其慈子、耆利，不同禽獸者亡幾耳。

translations.literal: Their loving children and craving profit—not differing from birds and beasts is but little.
translations.idiomatic: parental tenderness there is, but it is love of gain; they stand barely a hair's breadth above the beasts.

sentences.zh: 今其遺見餘俗，猶尚未改，棄禮誼，捐廉恥日甚，可謂月異而歲不同矣。

translations.literal: Now its leftover legacy and surviving customs have still not yet changed; casting aside ritual and righteousness, throwing away integrity and shame daily more extreme—it can be called month different and year not the same.
translations.idiomatic: The foul habits Qin left behind linger still: ritual and right are abandoned, honor is shed, and the decline worsens by the month until the year is unrecognizable.

sentences.zh: 逐利不耳，慮非顧行也；

translations.literal: They pursue profit and nothing else; they do not consider or look to conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Profit is all they hear; decency never enters the reckoning;

sentences.zh: 今其甚者殺父兄矣。

translations.literal: Now in the extreme cases they kill fathers and elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: until some go so far as to murder father or brother.

sentences.zh: 而大臣特以簿書不報、期會之間以為大故，至於俗流失，世壞敗，因恬而不知怪，慮不動於耳目，以為是適然耳。

translations.literal: Yet great ministers take only that ledgers are not reported and between deadline meetings as the great matter; as for custom flowing away and the age ruined and defeated, they are calm thereby and do not know it strange; care is not moved in ear and eye—they think this is only fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Yet high ministers fuss only over late paperwork and missed deadlines, as if those were the gravest crises. When custom rots and society crumbles, they remain placid and call it normal, for nothing their eyes or ears report seems worth a second thought.

sentences.zh: 夫移風易俗，使天下回心而鄉道，類非俗吏之所能為也。

translations.literal: Now to shift custom and change vulgar ways, causing all under Heaven to turn heart and incline to the Way—in kind is not what vulgar clerks can do.
translations.idiomatic: To shift the wind of custom and turn the empire's heart toward the Way is not work for petty bureaucrats.

sentences.zh: 俗吏之所務，在於刀筆、筐篋而不知大體。

translations.literal: What vulgar clerks attend to lies in knife-brush and basket-box, and they do not know the great substance.
translations.idiomatic: Such men live for their brush cases and document satchels; they have no grasp of the larger pattern.

sentences.zh: 陛下又不自憂，竊為陛下惜之！

translations.literal: Your Majesty again does not worry for yourself—your servant privately pities this for Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty will not even trouble yourself over it, I can only grieve in private!

sentences.zh: 豈如今定經制，令君君、臣臣，上下有差，父子六親各得其宜。

translations.literal: How about now fixing the classics and system, ordering lord lord and minister minister, high and low having gradation, father and son and six kin each obtaining their fitness.
translations.idiomatic: Better to fix the fundamental laws now: true sovereignty above, true service below, clear ranks from top to bottom, every family relationship in its proper place.

sentences.zh: 此業壹定，世世常安，而後有所持循矣；

translations.literal: Once this enterprise is fixed, age after age there is constant peace, and afterward there is something to hold and follow.
translations.idiomatic: Once that settlement is made, peace can pass down the generations, and posterity will have a model to follow;

sentences.zh: 若夫經制不定，是猶渡江河亡維楫，中流而遇風波，船必覆矣。

translations.literal: If the classics and system are not fixed, it is like crossing rivers and seas without ropes and oars—midstream meeting wind and waves, the boat must capsize.
translations.idiomatic: leave the basic order unsettled and you cross a great river without oar or rudder: meet a squall midstream and the vessel must founder.

sentences.zh: 可為長太息者此也。

translations.literal: What may be long sighed for is this.
translations.idiomatic: This too is cause for one of the six long sighs.

sentences.zh: :夏、殷、周為天子皆數十世，秦為天子二世而亡。

translations.literal: : Xia, Yin, and Zhou as Sons of Heaven each for several tens of generations; Qin as Son of Heaven two generations and perished.
translations.idiomatic: : The Xia, Shang, and Zhou each held the mandate for dozens of reigns; Qin held it for two reigns and collapsed.

sentences.zh: 人性不甚相遠也，何三代之君有道之長而秦無道之暴也？

translations.literal: Human nature is not greatly distant from itself—why did the lords of the Three Ages have the Way and long endure, while Qin lacked the Way and was violent?
translations.idiomatic: Human nature has not changed much across the ages—so why did the rulers of the three ancient dynasties enjoy long, virtuous reigns while Qin's lack of the Way brought sudden ruin?

sentences.zh: 其故可知也。

translations.literal: Its reason can be known.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is not hard to see.

sentences.zh: 古之王者，太子乃生，固舉以禮，有司齊肅端冕，見之南郊，過闕則下，過廟則趨，故自為赤子，而教固已行矣。

translations.literal: The kings of antiquity: when the heir apparent was just born, solidly they raised him with ritual; officials fasting and solemn with straight caps and robes showed him at the southern suburb; passing a tower gate then dismounting, passing a temple then hurrying—therefore from being a red child, instruction was already practiced.
translations.idiomatic: The kings of old, as soon as the heir was born, received him with full ceremony: officers in fasting garb and formal regalia presented him at the southern suburb; he dismounted at the palace gate and quickened his step past the ancestral shrine—thus moral instruction began while he was still in swaddling clothes.

sentences.zh: 孩提有識，三公、三少明孝仁禮義以道習之，逐去邪人，不使見惡行，於是皆選天下之端士、孝悌博聞有道術者以衛翼之，使與太子居處出入。

translations.literal: When the child in arms had awareness, the three dukes and three juniors enlightened him in filiality, benevolence, ritual, and righteousness to guide and drill him, drove away wicked men, did not allow him to see evil conduct; thereupon all selected the realm's upright gentlemen, filial and fraternal, broadly learned and possessed of the Way and arts, to guard and wing him, causing them to dwell, rise, and go out with the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment the boy could understand speech, the six mentors drilled him in filial piety, humanity, ritual, and right, drove away corrupt companions, and shielded him from base example; the court then chose the finest scholars in the land—men of filial piety, wide learning, and proven principle—to attend the heir at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 故太子乃生而見正事，聞正言，行正道，左右前後皆正人也。

translations.literal: Therefore the heir apparent from birth saw correct affairs, heard correct words, walked correct paths; to left and right, before and behind, all were correct men.
translations.idiomatic: Thus from birth the crown prince saw only upright conduct, heard only upright speech, and walked only upright paths; every face around him belonged to a good man.

sentences.zh: 夫習與正人居之不能毋正，猶生長於齊不能不齊言也；

translations.literal: Now habit with correct men dwelling—one cannot but be correct, just as growing up in Qi one cannot but speak Qi speech;
translations.idiomatic: Live always among the upright and you cannot help becoming upright, just as a child raised in Qi cannot help speaking the Qi dialect;

sentences.zh: 習與不正人居之不能毋不正，猶生長於楚之地不能不楚言也。

translations.literal: habit with incorrect men dwelling—one cannot but be incorrect, just as growing up in Chu's land one cannot but speak Chu speech.
translations.idiomatic: dwell among the crooked and you will twist like them, as surely as a child of Chu speaks the Chu tongue.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『少成若天性，習貫如自然。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "What is formed in youth is like nature; habit drilled is like what is natural.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "What the boy learns in youth becomes second nature; habit hardens into instinct.

sentences.zh: 』習與智長，故切而不愧；

translations.literal: " Habit grows with wisdom, therefore cutting yet not ashamed;
translations.idiomatic: " Counsel grows sharper as his mind matures, so rebukes can be blunt without giving offense;

sentences.zh: 化與心成，故中道若性。

translations.literal: transformation completes with the heart, therefore hitting the Way is like nature.
translations.idiomatic: moral transformation fuses with his inner heart until the middle path feels as natural as instinct.

sentences.zh: 夫三代之所以長久者，以其輔翼太子有此具也。

translations.literal: Now why the Three Ages were long enduring lies in that their assisting and winging the heir apparent had these provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The three dynasties endured because they furnished the crown prince with exactly this support.

sentences.zh: 及秦而不然，使趙高傅胡亥而教之獄，所習者非斬、劓人，則夷人之三族也。

translations.literal: When it came to Qin it was not so: they made Zhao Gao tutor Huhai and taught him in the prison; what he practiced was not beheading and nose-cutting men, then exterminating men's three clans.
translations.idiomatic: Qin did the opposite: Zhao Gao was made tutor to Huhai and schooled him in the jail, where he learned nothing but beheadings, mutilations, and the extermination of whole clans.

sentences.zh: 胡亥今日即位而明日射人，忠諫者謂之誹謗，深計者謂之妖言，其視殺人若艾草菅然。

translations.literal: Huhai today ascended the throne and tomorrow shot men; loyal remonstrators were called slander, deep planners were called perverse speech—he regarded killing men as mugwort and rush grass.
