translations.idiomatic: Huhai took the throne one day and the next was shooting people; loyal counsel was labeled slander, thoughtful policy was labeled sedition, and he treated killing men like mowing weeds.

sentences.zh: 豈惟胡亥之性惡哉？

translations.literal: Was it only Huhai's nature that was wicked?
translations.idiomatic: Was Huhai's nature alone to blame?

sentences.zh: 彼其所以道之者非其理故也。

translations.literal: That by which they guided him was not its proper pattern—therefore.
translations.idiomatic: Those who guided him taught him what was not right.

sentences.zh: 鄙諺曰：『前車覆，後車誡。

translations.literal: A rustic proverb says: "The front cart overturns; the rear cart takes warning.
translations.idiomatic: A common proverb runs, "When the lead wagon spills, the wagon behind should beware.

sentences.zh: 』秦世之所以亟絕者，其轍跡可見也；

translations.literal: " Why the Qin age was quickly cut off—the rut tracks can be seen;
translations.idiomatic: " Why Qin fell so swiftly is written clear as wagon ruts in the mud;

sentences.zh: 然而不避，是後車又將覆也。

translations.literal: yet not avoiding them—this is the rear cart again about to overturn.
translations.idiomatic: yet we swerve aside from none of its mistakes—the second wagon is about to overturn.

sentences.zh: 天下之命，縣於太子，太子之善，在於早諭教與選左右。

translations.literal: The fate of all under Heaven hangs on the heir apparent; the heir apparent's excellence lies in early instruction and selecting those to left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The fate of the empire hangs from the crown prince; his worth depends on early teaching and careful choice of companions.

sentences.zh: 夫心未濫而先諭都，則化易成也；

translations.literal: Now if before the heart is dissolute one first instructs Du, then transformation is easy to complete;
translations.idiomatic: Instruct the heart before passions run wild and moral transformation comes easily;

sentences.zh: 開於道術智誼之指，則教之力也；

translations.literal: opening him to the aims of the Way, arts, wisdom, and righteousness—then is the power of teaching.
translations.idiomatic: open his mind to the Way, to method, to wisdom and right—that is the true force of education;

sentences.zh: 若其服習積貫，則左右而已。

translations.literal: If it is a matter of clothing habit and accumulated practice, then it is only those to left and right.
translations.idiomatic: if you want lasting habit and inward conviction, nothing matters more than those who stand at his elbow.

sentences.zh: 夫胡、粵之人，生而同聲，嗜欲不異；

translations.literal: Now the men of Hu and Yue are born with the same cries; cravings and desires are not different;
translations.idiomatic: The Hu and the Yue are born with the same infant cry and the same appetites;

sentences.zh: 及其長而成俗，累數譯而不能相通，有雖死而不相為者，則教習然也。

translations.literal: when they have grown and customs form, piled translators cannot make them communicate; there are those who though dead do not act for each other—then it is teaching and habit that make it so.
translations.idiomatic: grown to manhood they grow so far apart that stacks of interpreters cannot bridge their speech, and men will die before aiding the other—all from upbringing and habit.

sentences.zh: 臣故曰選左右、早諭教最急。

translations.literal: Therefore your servant says selecting those to left and right and early instruction are most urgent.
translations.idiomatic: I repeat: choose his companions and begin his instruction early—nothing is more urgent.

sentences.zh: 夫教得而左右正，則太子正矣，太子正而天下定矣。

translations.literal: Now if teaching is obtained and those to left and right are correct, then the heir apparent is correct; the heir apparent is correct and all under Heaven is settled.
translations.idiomatic: When teaching succeeds and his attendants are upright, the heir becomes upright; when the heir is upright, the realm is settled.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：『一人有慶，兆民賴之。

translations.literal: The Documents says: "When one man has blessing, the myriad people rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says, "When the ruler knows blessing, the myriad people lean upon him.

sentences.zh: 』此時務也。

translations.literal: " This is the pressing task of the times.
translations.idiomatic: " That is the business of the hour.

sentences.zh: :凡人之智，能見已然，不能見將然。

translations.literal: : In general men's wisdom can see what is already so, cannot see what will be so.
translations.idiomatic: : Ordinary wit sees only what has already happened; it cannot see what is coming.

sentences.zh: 夫禮者禁於將然之前，而法者禁於已然之後，是故法之所為用易見而禮之所為生難知也。

translations.literal: Now ritual forbids before what will be so; law forbids after what is already so; therefore what law applies is easy to see, while what ritual does in giving birth is hard to know.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual stops wrong before it sprouts; law punishes wrong after the fact. The effects of law are obvious; the quiet work of ritual is easy to overlook.

sentences.zh: 若夫慶賞以勸善，刑罰以懲惡，先王執此之政，堅如金石；

translations.literal: As for rewards and grants to encourage good, punishments and fines to chastise evil—the former kings grasped this in government, firm as metal and stone;
translations.idiomatic: Rewards to encourage good and punishments to check evil—the ancient kings wielded both, unshakable as metal;

sentences.zh: 行此之令，信如四時；

translations.literal: carried out these orders, trustworthy as the four seasons;
translations.idiomatic: as reliable as the seasons;

sentences.zh: 據此之公，無私如天地，豈顧不用哉？

translations.literal: relied on this fairness, without private bias like Heaven and Earth—how could they have been unwilling to use them?
translations.idiomatic: as impartial as heaven and earth. Of course they used them—why would they not?

sentences.zh: 然而曰禮雲、禮雲者，貴絕惡於未萌而起教於微眇，使民日遷善、遠罪而不自知也。

translations.literal: Yet when it is said "ritual, ritual," what is prized is cutting off evil before it sprouts, and raising instruction in what is subtle and minute, causing the people day by day to move toward good and far from crime without themselves knowing it.
translations.idiomatic: When we speak of ritual, we mean killing evil in the bud and teaching in the finest grain of life, so the people drift toward goodness and away from crime without noticing the tug.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『聽訟，吾猶人也；

translations.literal: Confucius said: "In hearing lawsuits, I am like other men;
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "In hearing cases I am no wiser than other men;

sentences.zh: 必也使毋訟乎！

translations.literal: it must be to cause there to be no lawsuits!"
translations.idiomatic: what I want is to bring it about that there are no cases at all!"

sentences.zh: 』為人主計者，莫如先審取舍，取舍之極定於內而安危之萌應於外矣。

translations.literal: " For one who plans for the lord of men, nothing is like first examining what to take and what to reject; when the utmost of taking and rejecting is fixed within, then the sprouts of security and peril respond without.
translations.idiomatic: " For a ruler's counselor, nothing comes before weighing what to embrace and what to reject; once that choice is settled within, the seeds of safety or ruin appear without.

sentences.zh: 秦王之欲尊宗廟而安子孫，與湯、武同。

translations.literal: The King of Qin's desire to honor the ancestral temple and secure sons and grandsons was the same as Tang's and Wu's.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin king wanted to glorify his shrines and secure his line no less than Tang or Wu.

sentences.zh: 然而湯、武廣大其德行，六七百歲而弗失，秦王治天下十餘歲則大敗。

translations.literal: Yet Tang and Wu enlarged their virtue and conduct, six or seven hundred years and did not lose it; the King of Qin governed all under Heaven, and in over ten years there was great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Tang and Wu broadened their virtue and held the realm six or seven hundred years, while Qin's way collapsed in little more than a decade.

sentences.zh: 此亡他故矣：湯、武之定取舍審而秦王之定取舍不審矣。

translations.literal: This has no other reason: Tang and Wu's fixing of taking and rejecting was careful, while the King of Qin's fixing of taking and rejecting was not careful.
translations.idiomatic: No other cause lies beneath it: Tang and Wu chose their course with care, while the King of Qin chose his with blind recklessness.

sentences.zh: 夫天下，大器也；

translations.literal: Now all under Heaven is a great vessel.
translations.idiomatic: The empire is a great vessel;

sentences.zh: 今人之置器，置諸安處則安，置諸危處則危。

translations.literal: Now when men set a vessel, if they set it in a secure place it is secure; if they set it in a perilous place it is perilous.
translations.idiomatic: set a precious thing on a safe shelf and it stays whole; set it on a ledge over a cliff and it will shatter.

sentences.zh: 天下之情，與器無以異，在天子之所置之。

translations.literal: The disposition of all under Heaven does not differ from a vessel—it lies in where the Son of Heaven sets it.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is no different: everything depends on where the Son of Heaven places it.

sentences.zh: 湯、武置天下於仁、義、禮、樂，累子孫數十世，此天下所共聞也；

translations.literal: Tang and Wu set all under Heaven on benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music, piling sons and grandsons for several tens of generations—this all under Heaven jointly has heard;
translations.idiomatic: Tang and Wu set the realm on benevolence, right, ritual, and music, and their houses ruled dozens of generations—that story the whole world knows by heart;

sentences.zh: 秦王置天下於法令、刑罰，禍幾及身，子孫誅絕，此天下之所共見也。

translations.literal: The King of Qin set all under Heaven on laws, orders, punishments, and fines; calamity nearly reached his person, sons and grandsons were executed to extinction—this all under Heaven jointly has seen.
translations.idiomatic: the Qin king set the realm on statutes and the rack: disaster brushed his own skin, and his line was cut off root and branch—that spectacle everyone has seen with his own eyes.

sentences.zh: 是非其明效大驗邪！

translations.literal: Is this not its clear effect and great proof!
translations.idiomatic: Could proof be clearer or the lesson louder?

sentences.zh: 人之言曰：『聽言之道，必以其事觀之，則言者莫敢妄言。

translations.literal: Men's words say: "In the way of listening to words, one must observe them by their affairs—then those who speak dare not speak wildly.
translations.idiomatic: Men say, "Test every counsel against the facts, and no one will dare traffic in empty words.

sentences.zh: 』今或言禮誼之不如法令，教化之不如刑罰，人主胡不引殷、周、秦事以觀之也！

translations.literal: " Now some say ritual and righteousness are not as good as laws and orders, transformation and teaching not as good as punishments and fines—why does the lord of men not cite Yin, Zhou, and Qin affairs to observe it!
translations.idiomatic: " If anyone claims ritual cannot match statute or moral suasion the rack, let the ruler weigh the histories of Yin, Zhou, and Qin and judge for himself!

sentences.zh: 人主之尊譬如堂，群臣如陛，眾庶如地。

translations.literal: The lord of men's honor is like a hall; the host of ministers like steps; the multitude like the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's majesty is the high hall; his ministers are the stair; the common people are the earth below.

sentences.zh: 故陛九級上，廉遠地，則堂高；

translations.literal: Therefore when the steps are nine tiers up, the edge far from the ground, then the hall is high;
translations.idiomatic: Many tiers of steps lift the hall high above the ground;

sentences.zh: 陛無級，廉近地，則堂卑。

translations.literal: when the steps lack tiers, the edge near the ground, then the hall is low.
translations.idiomatic: strip away those steps and the hall sits almost in the dust.

sentences.zh: 高者難攀，卑者易陵，理勢然也。

translations.literal: What is high is hard to climb; what is low is easy to overrun—pattern and posture are thus.
translations.idiomatic: What stands high is hard to storm; what lies low invites trampling—that is simply how things work.

sentences.zh: 故古者聖王制為等列，內有公、卿、大夫、士，外有公、侯、伯、子、男，然後有官師、小吏，延及庶人，等級分明而天子加焉，故其尊不可及也。

translations.literal: Therefore in antiquity the sage kings made ranked arrays: within there were dukes, ministers, great officers, and knights; without there were dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons; afterward there were official masters and petty clerks, extending to the common people—grades and ranks were clear, and the Son of Heaven was added above them; therefore his honor could not be reached.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings built a ladder of rank—within the court from dukes down to ordinary knights, without from feudal princes down to petty clerks and then the people—each step distinct, with the Son of Heaven alone above them all. That is how his majesty became unapproachable.

sentences.zh: :里諺曰：『欲投鼠而忌器。

translations.literal: : A hamlet proverb says: "Desiring to throw at a rat yet fearing the vessel.
translations.idiomatic: : The proverb says, "You hesitate to strike the rat for fear of the vase beside it.

sentences.zh: 』此善諭也。

translations.literal: " This is a good analogy.
translations.idiomatic: " That is apt counsel.

sentences.zh: 鼠近於器，尚憚不投，恐傷其器，況於貴臣之近主乎！

translations.literal: When the rat is near the vessel, still one fears not to throw, fearing to harm the vessel—how much more for noble ministers near the lord!
translations.idiomatic: Even a rat beside a precious jar gives pause—how much more a high minister standing at the ruler's elbow!

sentences.zh: 廉恥節禮以治君子，故有賜死而亡戮辱。

translations.literal: With integrity, shame, restraint, and ritual they governed gentlemen; therefore there was granted death but no shame of execution.
translations.idiomatic: Integrity, shame, and ritual governed the gentleman class: they might be sentenced to die, but never dragged through public mutilation.

sentences.zh: 是以黥、劓之罪不及大夫，以其離主上不遠也。

translations.literal: Therefore branding and nose-cutting punishments did not reach great officers, because their distance from the lord above was not far.
translations.idiomatic: Branding and cropping never touched a grandee, for he stood too close to the throne.

sentences.zh: 禮：不敢齒君之路馬，蹴其芻者有罰，所以為主上豫遠不敬也。

translations.literal: By ritual one did not dare rank the lord's road horses; one who kicked their fodder had punishment—this was why for the lord above beforehand to keep far lack of respect.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual forbade even naming the age of the ruler's team horses; kick their fodder and you were fined—all to keep contempt at a distance from the ruler.

sentences.zh: 今自王、侯、三公之貴，皆天子之所改容而禮之也，古天子之所謂伯父、伯舅也；

translations.literal: Now from kings, marquises, and the three dukes' honor—all are those whom the Son of Heaven changes countenance and treats with ritual, what antiquity's Son of Heaven called uncle and elder uncle;
translations.idiomatic: Today kings, marquises, and the three dukes—men the emperor greets with altered mien, the very kin the ancients called uncle or great-uncle;

sentences.zh: 而令與眾庶同黥、劓、髡、刖、笞、傌、棄市之法，然則堂不無陛虖！

translations.literal: yet ordering them to share with the multitude branding, cropping, shaving, cutting off feet, flogging, exposure, and execution in the market—then is not the hall without its steps!
translations.idiomatic: are thrown to the same branding, cropping, shaving, hobbling, flogging, and public execution as common felons. Is that not tearing the steps from under the hall!

sentences.zh: 被戮辱者不泰迫虖！

translations.literal: Those who suffer execution and shame—are they not too pressed!
translations.idiomatic: Are not those who suffer such shame driven past endurance!

sentences.zh: 廉恥不行，大臣無乃握重權、大官而有徒隸無恥之心虖！

translations.literal: With integrity and shame not practiced, is it not that great ministers grasp heavy power, great offices yet have the heart of convicts and slaves without shame!
translations.idiomatic: When shame no longer restrains them, will not great officers who hold the levers of power begin to think like shackled slaves!

sentences.zh: 夫望夷之事，二世見當以重法者，投鼠而不忌器之習也。

translations.literal: Now as for the affair at Wangyi, when the Second Generation met judgment with heavy law—it was the habit of throwing at rats without fearing the vessel.
translations.idiomatic: The slaughter at Wangyi Palace, where the Second Emperor fell to harsh law, was the fruit of striking rats without regard for the vase.

sentences.zh: 臣聞之：履雖鮮不加於枕，冠雖敝不以苴履。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard: though shoes be fresh, they are not placed on the pillow; though the cap be worn, it is not used to plug shoes.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard it said: never put new shoes on the pillow, nor plug worn-out shoes with your cap—each thing keeps its proper use.

sentences.zh: 夫嘗已在貴寵之位，天子改容而禮貌之矣，吏民嘗俯伏以敬畏之矣；

translations.literal: Now for one who has already been in honored and favored rank, the Son of Heaven has changed countenance and treated him with ritual courtesy; clerks and people have bent low in awe and reverence;
translations.idiomatic: A man raised to high favor—whom the emperor has greeted with respect and whom officials and commoners have learned to revere—

sentences.zh: 今而有過，帝令廢之可也，退之可也，賜之死可也，滅之可也；

translations.literal: now if he has faults, the Emperor ordering him dismissed is acceptable, demoting him is acceptable, granting him death is acceptable, destroying him is acceptable;
translations.idiomatic: may be cashiered, demoted, sentenced to death, or his house destroyed if he sins;

sentences.zh: 若夫束縛之，系媟之，輸之司寇，編之徒官，司寇小吏詈罵而榜笞之，殆非所以令眾庶見也。

translations.literal: but as for binding him, tying him with insult, handing him to the Minister of Justice, enrolling him among convict officials, Minister of Justice petty clerks reviling and flogging him—this is almost not the means by which to let the multitude see.
translations.idiomatic: but to bind him, drag him in disgrace to the Minister of Justice, register him with the convict labor corps, and let petty jailers curse and flog him—that is no sight for the people to witness.

sentences.zh: 夫卑賤者習知尊貴者之一旦吾亦乃可以加此也，非所以尊尊、貴貴之化也。

translations.literal: Now the base and vile habitually know that for the honored and noble, one day "I too then can apply this to them"—this is not the means of the transformation of honoring the honored and esteeming the noble.
translations.idiomatic: Low folk will learn that even the mighty may one day be treated so—that trains the realm in contempt, not in reverence for rank.

sentences.zh: 古者大臣有坐不廉而廢者，不謂不廉，曰簠簋不飾』；

translations.literal: In antiquity when great officers sat guilty of not being incorrupt and were dismissed, they were not called not incorrupt, but said "the gui vessels are not adorned";
translations.idiomatic: When a great officer was removed for corruption, the court did not call it corruption; it said his "sacrificial vessels lacked proper polish";

sentences.zh: 坐污穢淫亂、男女無別者，不曰污穢，曰『帷薄不修』；

translations.literal: when sitting guilty of filth, promiscuity, and men and women without distinction, they were not called filthy, but said "screen curtains not repaired";
translations.idiomatic: when charged with sexual scandal, they spoke of "slack inner curtains" instead of naming the filth;

sentences.zh: 坐罷軟不勝任者，不謂罷軟，曰『下官不職』。

translations.literal: when sitting guilty of weak slackness and not bearing office, they were not called weak slack, but said "lower officials not performing duty."
translations.idiomatic: when removed for incompetence, they blamed "subordinate officers" rather than call him weak.

sentences.zh: 故貴大臣定有其罪矣，猶未斥然正以呼之也，尚遷就而為之諱也。

translations.literal: Therefore though honored great officers definitely had their guilt, still they did not openly and straight call it, still bent and accommodated and for them concealed it.
translations.idiomatic: Even when guilt was fixed, the court still wrapped the fault in euphemism rather than shout the crime aloud.

sentences.zh: 故其在大譴、大何之域者，聞譴、何則白冠氂纓，盤水加劍，造請室而請罪耳，上不執縛系引而行也；

translations.literal: Therefore those in the region of great reproach and great fault—when they heard reproach and fault then white cap ram's-hair tassels, basin of water with sword laid on, went to the plea chamber and pled guilt, that is all; those above did not seize, bind, tie, and lead them to go.
translations.idiomatic: For grave faults the minister donned white mourning garb, carried sword across a basin of water, and presented himself in the plea chamber; the emperor did not send guards to drag him in chains.

sentences.zh: 其有中罪者，聞命而自弛，上不使人頸盭而加也；

translations.literal: Those with middle guilt, hearing the order then themselves loosened; those above did not cause men to twist the neck and apply.
translations.idiomatic: For middling crimes he removed his own insignia at the order; no bailiff wrenched his collar or forced the halter on him;

sentences.zh: 其有大罪者，聞命則北面再拜，跪而自裁，上不使人捽抑而刑之也。

translations.literal: Those with great guilt, on hearing the order then faced north and bowed twice, knelt and executed themselves; those above did not have men seize, press down, and punish them.
translations.idiomatic: For the gravest crimes the minister, on receiving the order, faced north, bowed twice, knelt, and took his own life; the emperor did not send men to seize him, wrestle him down, and apply the rack.

sentences.zh: 曰：『子大夫自有過耳，吾遇子有禮矣。

translations.literal: He said: "You, grandee, have your own faults—We treated you with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: He would say, "You, sir, were at fault—but I treated you with ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 』遇之有禮，故群臣自熹；

translations.literal: " Treating them with propriety, therefore the host of ministers rejoiced of themselves;
translations.idiomatic: " Because the ruler met them with propriety, the ministers took heart of themselves;

sentences.zh: 嬰以廉恥，故人矜節行。

translations.literal: They cherished integrity and shame, therefore men prized conduct and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: they were nurtured in integrity and shame, and men therefore prized upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 上設廉恥、禮義以遇其臣不以節行報其上者，則非人類也。

translations.literal: When the ruler set up integrity, shame, ritual, and righteousness to meet his ministers—whoever did not repay his lord with conduct and integrity was not of the human kind.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler established integrity, shame, ritual, and right to treat his ministers, anyone who failed to repay his lord with upright conduct was scarcely human.

sentences.zh: 故化成俗定，則為人臣者皆顧行而忘利，守節而伏義，故可以托不御之權，可以寄六尺之孤，此厲廉恥、行禮誼之所致也，主上何喪焉！

translations.literal: Therefore when transformation completed and custom was fixed, those who served as ministers all looked to conduct and forgot profit, kept integrity and submitted to righteousness—therefore one could entrust authority without reins, could deposit a six-foot orphan; this is what urging integrity and shame and practicing ritual and righteousness brought about—what has the lord above lost!
translations.idiomatic: Once custom was formed and fixed, ministers thought of conduct and forgot profit, kept their integrity and bowed to right; then one could entrust unchecked authority and commit a fatherless child six feet tall to their care—that is what fostering integrity and shame and practicing ritual and right achieves. What has the ruler lost!

sentences.zh: 此之不為而顧彼之久行，故曰可為長太息者此也。

translations.literal: To neglect this and instead attend to that long practiced—therefore it is said what may be long sighed for is this.
translations.idiomatic: To leave this undone while clinging to what has long been practiced—this too is cause for one of the six long sighs.

sentences.zh: 誼以絳侯前逮繫獄，卒無事，故以此譏上。

translations.literal: Yi, because the Marquis of Jiang had formerly been arrested and imprisoned yet in the end had no affair, therefore used this to reproach the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi cited how the Marquis of Jiang had once been arrested and jailed yet came to no harm, and used that episode to reproach the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上深納其言，養臣下有節，是後大臣有罪，皆自殺，不受刑。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply took in his words, nurtured ministers below with propriety; after this when great ministers were guilty, all killed themselves and did not accept punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his counsel deeply to heart and treated his ministers with ritual propriety; thereafter guilty great ministers all took their own lives rather than submit to punishment.

sentences.zh: ----1冬，十月，令列侯太夫人、夫人、諸侯王子及吏二千石無得擅征捕。

translations.literal: ----1 In winter, the tenth month, an order: the great ladies and ladies of marquises, princes of feudal lords, and officials of two thousand piculs were not to arrest or seize on their own authority.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In winter, the tenth month, an edict forbade the great ladies and consorts of marquises, feudal princes, and officials of two thousand piculs from arresting anyone on their own authority.

sentences.zh: ----2夏，四月，赦天下。

translations.literal: ----2 In summer, the fourth month, a general amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In summer, the fourth month, the emperor amnestied all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: ----3六月，癸酉，未央宮東闕罘罳災。

translations.literal: ----3 In the sixth month, on guiyou, the screen curtains of the eastern tower gate of Weiyang Palace caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In the sixth month, on guiyou, fire destroyed the screen curtains at the eastern tower gate of Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: ----4民有歌淮南王者曰：「一尺布，尚可縫；

translations.literal: ----4 Among the people was one who sang of the King of Huainan, saying, "A foot of cloth can still be sewn;
translations.idiomatic: ----4 The people sang of the King of Huainan: "A foot of cloth can still be sewn;

sentences.zh: 一斗粟，尚可舂；

translations.literal: a peck of grain can still be husked;
translations.idiomatic: a peck of grain can still be husked;

sentences.zh: 兄弟二人不相容！

translations.literal: two brothers cannot dwell together!"
translations.idiomatic: two brothers cannot dwell together!"

sentences.zh: 」帝聞而病之。

translations.literal: " The emperor heard and was pained by it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor heard it and was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: ----1夏，封淮南厲王子安等四人為列侯。

translations.literal: ----1 In summer, he enfeoffed An and three others, sons of the Lamented King of Huainan, as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In summer, he enfeoffed Liu An and three other sons of the Lamented King of Huainan as marquises.

sentences.zh: 賈誼知上必將復王之也，上疏諫曰：「淮南王之悖逆無道，天下孰不知其罪！

translations.literal: Jia Yi knew the emperor would surely restore him as king; he submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying, "The King of Huainan's perverse rebellion against the Way—who under Heaven does not know his guilt!
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi knew the emperor would surely restore him as king; he submitted a memorial remonstrating: "The King of Huainan's perverse rebellion against the Way—who under Heaven does not know his guilt!

sentences.zh: 陛下幸而赦遷之，自疾而死，天下孰以王死之不噹！

translations.literal: Your Majesty graciously pardoned and banished him; he died of illness on his own—who under Heaven will say the king's death was undeserved!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty graciously pardoned and banished him; he died of his own illness—who under Heaven will say the king's death was undeserved!

sentences.zh: 今奉尊罪人之子，適足以負謗於天下耳。

translations.literal: Now to honor and elevate a guilty man's son is only enough to bear slander from all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Now to honor and elevate a guilty man's son is only enough to earn slander from all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 此人少壯，豈能忘其父哉！

translations.literal: This man is young and in his prime—how could he forget his father!
translations.idiomatic: This man is young and in his prime—how could he forget his father!

sentences.zh: 白公勝所為父報仇者，大父與叔父也。

translations.literal: What Duke Bai Sheng did to avenge his father was against his grandfather and his father's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Bai Sheng avenged his father upon his grandfather and his uncle.

sentences.zh: 白公為亂，非欲取國代主，發忿快志，剡手以沖仇人之匈，固為俱靡而已。

translations.literal: Duke Bai raised disorder—not desiring to take the state and replace the lord, but venting wrath and satisfying will, drawing hand to pierce the enemy's breast—fundamentally it was only to perish together.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Bai raised rebellion not to seize the state and replace his lord, but to vent his rage and satisfy his will—to drive his hand into the enemy's breast and perish together.

sentences.zh: 淮南雖小，黥布嘗用之矣，漢存，特幸耳。

translations.literal: Though Huainan is small, Qing Bu once used it; Han survives only by special fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Though Huainan is small, Qing Bu once made use of it; Han survives only by special fortune.

sentences.zh: 夫擅仇人足以危漢之資，於策不便。

translations.literal: Now to grant a man who harbors enmity resources enough to endanger Han is in policy not advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: To arm a man who harbors enmity with resources enough to endanger Han is poor policy.

sentences.zh: 予之眾，積之財，此非有子胥、白公報於廣都之中，即疑有專諸、荊軻起於兩柱之間，所謂假賊兵，為虎翼者也。

translations.literal: Give him troops, pile up wealth for him—if this is not having Zixu or Duke Bai take revenge in the broad capital, then one suspects having Zhuan Zhu or Jing Ke rise between the two pillars; it is what is called lending arms to bandits and giving wings to a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: Give him troops and pile up wealth for him—if this is not to breed another Zixu or Duke Bai taking revenge in the capital, it is to risk another Zhuan Zhu or Jing Ke rising between the palace pillars; it is what men call lending arms to bandits and giving wings to a tiger.

sentences.zh: 願陛下少留計！

translations.literal: Your Majesty, we beg you to pause and consider!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, I beg you to pause and reconsider!

sentences.zh: 」上弗聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: ----2有長星出於東方。

translations.literal: ----2 A long comet appeared in the east.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 A long comet appeared in the east.

translations.idiomatic: ----1 In spring, a great drought.

sentences.zh: ----1冬，上行幸甘泉。

translations.literal: ----1 In winter, the emperor traveled in person to Sweet Springs.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In winter, the emperor traveled in person to Sweet Springs.

sentences.zh: ----2將軍薄昭殺漢使者。

translations.literal: ----2 General Bo Zhao killed a Han envoy.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 General Bo Zhao killed a Han envoy.

sentences.zh: 帝不忍加誅，使公卿從之飲酒。

translations.literal: The emperor could not bear to execute him and had the high ministers drink with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not bear to execute him outright and had the high ministers drink with him.

sentences.zh: 欲令自引分，昭不肯；

translations.literal: He wished to cause him to take his own portion of blame; Zhao refused;
translations.idiomatic: He hoped Zhao would take his own life; Zhao refused;

sentences.zh: 使群臣喪服往哭之，乃自殺。

translations.literal: he had the host of ministers go in mourning garb to wail for him—then Zhao killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: he sent the ministers in mourning garb to wail for him—then Zhao killed himself.

sentences.zh: ::臣光曰：李德裕以為：「漢文帝誅薄昭，斷則明矣，於義則未安也。

translations.literal: :: Your servant Guang says: Li Deyu held that "Emperor Wen of Han executed Bo Zhao—decisive, it was clear; in righteousness, it was not settled.
translations.idiomatic: :: Your servant Guang says: Li Deyu held that "Emperor Wen of Han executed Bo Zhao—decisive, it was clear; in righteousness, it was not settled.

sentences.zh: 秦康送晉文，興如存之感；

translations.literal: Duke Kang of Qin escorted Duke Wen of Jin—the stirring was as if he still lived;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Kang of Qin escorted Duke Wen of Jin—the stirring was as if he still lived;

sentences.zh: 況太后尚存，唯一弟薄昭，斷之不疑，非所以慰母氏之心也。

translations.literal: how much more when the empress dowager still lived and Bo Zhao was her only brother—to cut him off without doubt was not the means to comfort the mother's heart.
translations.idiomatic: how much more when the empress dowager still lived and Bo Zhao was her only brother—to cut him off without hesitation was no comfort to a mother's heart.

sentences.zh: 」臣愚以為法者天下之公器，惟善持法者，親疏如一，無所不行，則人莫敢有所恃而犯之也。

translations.literal: " Your servant is foolish and holds that law is the public vessel of all under Heaven; only one skilled at holding law treats kin and stranger as one, applies it everywhere without exception—then no man dares rely on anything and transgress it.
translations.idiomatic: " Your servant holds that law is the public instrument of all under Heaven; only one skilled at upholding law treats kin and stranger alike and applies it without exception—then no one dares rely on favor and transgress it.

sentences.zh: 夫薄昭雖素稱長者，文帝不為置賢師傅而用之典兵；

translations.literal: Now though Bo Zhao was always called a worthy elder, Emperor Wen did not set up worthy teachers and tutors for him but used him to command troops;
translations.idiomatic: Though Bo Zhao was always called a worthy elder, Emperor Wen did not assign him worthy teachers and tutors but used him to command troops;

sentences.zh: 驕而犯上，至於殺漢使者，非有恃而然乎！

translations.literal: proud and transgressing against his superiors, reaching the point of killing a Han envoy—is this not having something to rely on and therefore becoming so!
translations.idiomatic: grew proud, transgressed against his superiors, and killed a Han envoy—did he not act so because he had something to rely on!

sentences.zh: 若又從而赦之，則與成、哀之世何異哉！

translations.literal: If one again followed by pardoning him, how would it differ from the age of Cheng and Ai!
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor then pardoned him, how would that differ from the age of Cheng and Ai!

sentences.zh: 魏文帝嘗稱漢文帝之美，而不取其殺薄昭，曰：「-{舅后}-之家，但當養育以恩而不當假藉以權，既觸罪法，又不得不害。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei once praised Emperor Wen of Han's excellence yet did not approve his killing Bo Zhao, saying, "The house of -{舅后}- should only be nurtured with kindness and must not be lent authority; once they touch the penal law, one again cannot but harm them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei once praised Emperor Wen of Han's excellence yet did not approve his killing Bo Zhao, saying, "The house of -{舅后}- should only be nurtured with kindness and must not be lent authority; once they touch the penal law, one cannot but punish them.

sentences.zh: 」譏文帝之始不防閒昭也，斯言得之矣。

translations.literal: " He reproached Emperor Wen for not guarding against Bo Zhao at the start—this saying hits the mark.
translations.idiomatic: " He reproached Emperor Wen for not guarding against Bo Zhao at the start—this saying hits the mark.

sentences.zh: 然則欲慰母心者，將慎之於始乎！

translations.literal: If so, one who wishes to comfort a mother's heart will be careful at the beginning!
translations.idiomatic: If so, one who wishes to comfort a mother's heart must be careful at the beginning!
